domains.name: exploration
domains.description: Manages all mineral exploration and resource discovery activities including geological surveys, drilling programs, sampling, assay results, resource estimation, and JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC-compliant resource and reserve reporting. Owns exploration licenses, prospect data, drill-hole collars, and resource classification.

products.name: prospect
products.description: Master record for each exploration prospect or target area identified during mineral exploration programs. Captures prospect name, centroid coordinates (latitude/longitude and local grid), commodity targets, discovery date, exploration stage (grassroots, advanced, feasibility), geological province, structural domain, tenement reference, and current status (active, dormant, relinquished, converted to mining). Serves as the top-level spatial and business anchor for all exploration activities, drill programs, resource estimates, and regulatory reporting within a defined area of interest.

attributes.name: emergency_response_plan_id

attributes.name: area_hectares

attributes.name: centroid_latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the prospect centroid in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum).

attributes.name: centroid_longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the prospect centroid in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum).

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Name and specification of the coordinate reference system used for local grid coordinates (e.g., MGA Zone 50, UTM Zone 31N).

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: cutoff_grade_percent

attributes.name: discovery_date

attributes.name: drill_hole_count

attributes.name: environmental_clearance_status
attributes.description: Status of environmental impact assessment and regulatory clearance for exploration activities in the prospect area.

attributes.name: estimated_grade_percent

attributes.name: estimated_tonnage_mt
attributes.description: Current estimated total tonnage of mineralized material in the prospect, expressed in million tonnes. Confidential business data.

attributes.name: exploration_stage
attributes.description: Current stage of exploration maturity for the prospect, ranging from early-stage grassroots to advanced feasibility studies.

attributes.name: geological_confidence

attributes.name: geological_province
attributes.description: Name of the regional geological province or terrane in which the prospect is located.
attributes.references: Geological Survey Standards, Regional Geology Framework

attributes.name: last_drill_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent drilling activity conducted in the prospect.

attributes.name: last_resource_estimate_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent mineral resource estimate prepared for this prospect.

attributes.name: local_grid_easting
attributes.description: Easting coordinate of the prospect centroid in the local mine grid or project coordinate system, measured in meters.
attributes.references: Mine Survey and Spatial Data Standard

attributes.name: local_grid_northing
attributes.description: Northing coordinate of the prospect centroid in the local mine grid or project coordinate system, measured in meters.
attributes.references: Mine Survey and Spatial Data Standard

attributes.name: mineralization_style
attributes.description: Type or style of mineralization present in the prospect (e.g., porphyry, epithermal, sediment-hosted, banded iron formation, pegmatite).

attributes.name: next_planned_activity
attributes.description: Description of the next planned exploration activity or program for the prospect (e.g., drilling campaign, geophysical survey, feasibility study).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or comments about the prospect that do not fit structured fields.

attributes.name: prospect_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned to the prospect for identification in exploration systems and reporting.

attributes.name: prospect_name
attributes.description: Business name or designation of the exploration prospect or target area.

attributes.name: prospect_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the exploration prospect in its lifecycle.

attributes.name: reserve_classification
attributes.description: Highest level of ore reserve classification achieved for this prospect under JORC, NI 43-101, or SAMREC standards. None if no reserve has been declared.

attributes.name: resource_classification
attributes.description: Highest level of mineral resource classification achieved for this prospect under JORC, NI 43-101, or SAMREC standards. None if no resource has been estimated.

attributes.name: structural_domain
attributes.description: Structural geological domain or zone characterizing the prospect area (e.g., fault block, fold belt, shear zone).

attributes.name: target_depth_max_m
attributes.description: Maximum depth below surface at which mineralization is targeted or expected, measured in meters.

attributes.name: target_depth_min_m
attributes.description: Minimum depth below surface at which mineralization is targeted or expected, measured in meters.

attributes.name: total_meters_drilled
attributes.description: Cumulative total length of all drilling completed in the prospect, measured in meters.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this prospect record was last modified in the system.

products.name: licence
products.description: Master register of all exploration licences, permits, and tenements held for mineral exploration activities. Tracks licence number, issuing jurisdiction and regulatory authority, grant date, expiry date, renewal history, area in hectares/km², commodity rights granted, minimum expenditure commitments by year, security/bond requirements, reporting obligations, and regulatory conditions. Links to the tenement domain for broader land access context. Scoped exclusively to exploration-phase tenure — mining leases and production rights are owned by the tenement domain.

attributes.name: licence_id
attributes.description: Primary key for licence

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Exploration licences are cost centres for statutory expenditure tracking. Finance links licences to cost centres for minimum expenditure compliance reporting and regulatory audit trails.

attributes.name: counterparty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.counterparty. Business justification: Mining licences are frequently held under joint venture arrangements with an external counterparty as operator or co-holder. Linking licence to counterparty enables JV partner management, expenditure

attributes.name: environmental_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.environmental_permit. Business justification: Exploration licences operate under a governing environmental permit issued by the same regulatory authority. Licence compliance reporting and renewal submissions require direct reference to the enviro

attributes.name: profit_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_centre. Business justification: Exploration licences are assigned to profit centres for exploration accounting segment classification under IFRS 6 area-of-interest accounting. Mining finance requires profit centre on licences to cor

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Exploration licences ARE tenements in mining regulatory frameworks. Direct link enables statutory reporting, expenditure compliance tracking, and regulatory obligation management. Licence_number maps

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Exploration licences have statutory minimum expenditure commitments tracked against WBS elements for regulatory compliance reporting. Mining companies must demonstrate minimum spend per licence period

attributes.name: annual_rent_fee
attributes.description: Annual rental or holding fee payable to the regulatory authority to maintain the exploration licence. Typically calculated per hectare or as a flat fee.

attributes.name: application_date
attributes.description: Date on which the original application for the exploration licence was submitted to the regulatory authority.

attributes.name: area_square_km
attributes.description: Total surface area covered by the exploration licence measured in square kilometres. Alternative measurement for international reporting and comparison.

attributes.name: commodity_rights
attributes.description: List of minerals and commodities for which exploration rights have been granted under this licence. May include iron ore, copper, gold, lithium, nickel, coal, or all minerals depending on jurisdiction.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this exploration licence record was first created in the data platform.

attributes.name: environmental_approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether separate environmental impact assessment or approval is required before commencing exploration activities. True if required, False otherwise.

attributes.name: expenditure_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all expenditure commitment amounts. Ensures consistent financial reporting across jurisdictions.

attributes.name: heritage_site_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the licence area contains or overlaps with registered cultural heritage sites, archaeological sites, or sacred sites. True if heritage sites are present, False otherwise.

attributes.name: holder_registration_number
attributes.description: Company registration number, business number, or other official identifier of the licence holder as registered with the corporate regulator.

attributes.name: joint_venture_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the exploration licence is held under a joint venture arrangement with multiple parties. True if joint venture, False if sole holder.

attributes.name: last_renewal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the exploration licence was most recently renewed. Null if the licence has never been renewed.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this exploration licence record was most recently modified in the data platform.

attributes.name: maximum_renewals_allowed
attributes.description: Maximum number of renewals permitted under the applicable mining legislation. Once reached, the licence cannot be renewed further and must either be converted to a mining lease or surrendered.

attributes.name: minimum_expenditure_commitment_year_1
attributes.description: Mandatory minimum exploration expenditure required in the first year of the licence term to maintain tenure. Failure to meet this commitment may result in penalties or licence forfeiture.

attributes.name: minimum_expenditure_commitment_year_2
attributes.description: Mandatory minimum exploration expenditure required in the second year of the licence term to maintain tenure.

attributes.name: minimum_expenditure_commitment_year_3
attributes.description: Mandatory minimum exploration expenditure required in the third year of the licence term to maintain tenure.

attributes.name: minimum_expenditure_commitment_year_4
attributes.description: Mandatory minimum exploration expenditure required in the fourth year of the licence term to maintain tenure.

attributes.name: minimum_expenditure_commitment_year_5
attributes.description: Mandatory minimum exploration expenditure required in the fifth year of the licence term to maintain tenure.

attributes.name: next_reporting_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the next regulatory report or expenditure statement is due. Critical for compliance tracking and avoiding penalties.

attributes.name: regulatory_conditions
attributes.description: Special conditions, restrictions, or obligations imposed by the regulatory authority as part of the licence grant. May include environmental protection measures, heritage site restrictions, or community consultation requirements.

attributes.name: renewal_count
attributes.description: Number of times the exploration licence has been renewed since original grant. Used to track tenure history and assess remaining renewal opportunities.

attributes.name: renewal_eligibility_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the exploration licence is eligible for renewal based on compliance with expenditure commitments and regulatory conditions. True if eligible, False if not.

attributes.name: rent_fee_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the annual rent fee.

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which exploration activity reports and expenditure statements must be submitted to the regulatory authority.

attributes.name: security_bond_amount
attributes.description: Financial security or bond amount required to be lodged with the regulatory authority to cover potential rehabilitation costs and ensure compliance with licence conditions.

attributes.name: security_bond_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the security bond amount.

products.name: drill_hole
products.description: Master record for every drill hole (collar) executed across all exploration and resource definition programs. Captures hole ID (unique collar identifier), prospect reference, drill program reference, drill type (RC, diamond core, RAB, aircore, percussion), collar coordinates (easting, northing, RL in local mine grid and WGS84), planned and actual azimuth, planned and actual dip, planned and actual total depth, start date, completion date, drilling contractor, rig identifier, hole purpose (exploration, infill, geotechnical, sterilisation, hydrogeological), and hole status (planned, in-progress, completed, abandoned). The authoritative SSOT for drill hole identity and spatial metadata used by geology, laboratory, and resource estimation workflows.

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the drill hole collar record. Primary key for the drill hole entity.

attributes.name: asset_id
attributes.description: The unique identifier of the drilling rig used to execute this hole. Used for rig utilization tracking, maintenance correlation, and quality control. Typically the contractors rig fleet number or name.

attributes.name: drill_program_id
attributes.description: Reference to the drilling campaign or program under which this hole was executed. Used for budget tracking, contractor assignment, and program-level reporting.

attributes.name: hazard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.hazard. Business justification: Drill holes can intersect specific geological hazards (pressurized gas zones, H2S, unstable ground). Mining operations require drill holes to reference the identified hazard for safety management, inc

attributes.name: prospect_id
attributes.description: Reference to the exploration prospect or tenement where this drill hole is located. Links the hole to the broader exploration project and land package.

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Individual drill holes may be tied to specific PO line items for detailed cost tracking, invoicing reconciliation, and cost-per-meter analysis. Enables accurate job costing and dispute resolution with

attributes.name: target_commodity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: Individual drill holes target specific commodities - determines sampling protocol, assay suite selection, and QAQC standards (e.g., gold requires fire assay, base metals use multi-element ICP). Normal

attributes.name: abandonment_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for early termination or abandonment of the drill hole. Common reasons include equipment failure, ground conditions (cavity, water ingress), deviation beyond acceptable limits, or program budget constraints. Populated only when hole_status is abandoned.

attributes.name: actual_azimuth
attributes.description: The actual measured horizontal direction of the drill hole at the collar, measured in degrees clockwise from grid north (0-360). Captured from downhole survey or collar survey after drilling commences. May differ from planned azimuth due to setup adjustments or ground conditions.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Drilling Standard

attributes.name: actual_depth
attributes.description: The actual total depth achieved by the drill hole measured along the hole trajectory from collar to end-of-hole, measured in meters. May differ from planned depth due to early termination, ground conditions, or program adjustments.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Drilling Standard

attributes.name: actual_dip
attributes.description: The actual measured vertical angle of the drill hole at the collar, measured in degrees from horizontal. Captured from downhole survey or collar survey after drilling commences. May differ from planned dip due to setup adjustments or ground conditions.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Drilling Standard

attributes.name: collar_easting
attributes.description: The easting (X) coordinate of the drill hole collar in the local mine grid coordinate system, measured in meters. This is the authoritative spatial reference for the hole location used in resource modeling and mine planning.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Local Mine Grid Standard

attributes.name: collar_latitude
attributes.description: The latitude of the drill hole collar in WGS84 geographic coordinate system, measured in decimal degrees. Used for global positioning, regulatory reporting, and integration with external GIS systems.

attributes.name: collar_longitude
attributes.description: The longitude of the drill hole collar in WGS84 geographic coordinate system, measured in decimal degrees. Used for global positioning, regulatory reporting, and integration with external GIS systems.

attributes.name: collar_northing
attributes.description: The northing (Y) coordinate of the drill hole collar in the local mine grid coordinate system, measured in meters. Used in conjunction with easting and RL to define the three-dimensional collar position.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Local Mine Grid Standard

attributes.name: collar_rl
attributes.description: The elevation (Z) coordinate of the drill hole collar in the local mine grid coordinate system, measured in meters above the site datum. RL (Reduced Level) is the mining industry standard term for elevation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Local Mine Grid Standard

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: General free-text comments or notes about the drill hole, including operational issues, geological observations, or data quality notes. Used for contextual information that does not fit structured fields.

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: The date drilling operations were completed for this hole, including final survey and collar rehabilitation. Used for program reporting, contractor invoicing, and cycle time analysis.

attributes.name: core_diameter
attributes.description: The nominal diameter of the drill core recovered, applicable only to diamond core drilling. Standard sizes include PQ (85mm), HQ (63.5mm), NQ (47.6mm), BQ (36.4mm). Used for sample volume calculations and metallurgical testwork planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PQ|HQ|NQ|BQ|NQ2|HQ3|NMLC|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Diamond Drilling Standard

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this drill hole record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: drill_type
attributes.description: The drilling method used for this hole. RC (Reverse Circulation) provides chip samples; diamond core provides continuous core samples; RAB (Rotary Air Blast) and aircore are used for shallow reconnaissance; percussion and rotary are used for specific geological conditions; directional drilling is used for underground or complex geometries. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: RC|diamond_core|RAB|aircore|percussion|rotary|directional — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: hole_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the drill hole collar, typically assigned by the exploration team following site naming conventions. This is the externally-known collar identifier used in geological reports, assay certificates, and JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC resource statements.

attributes.name: hole_purpose
attributes.description: The primary objective of the drill hole. Exploration holes target new mineralization; infill holes increase resource confidence; geotechnical holes assess rock mechanics for mine design; sterilisation holes confirm absence of mineralization in infrastructure footprints; hydrogeological holes assess groundwater; metallurgical holes provide samples for processing testwork.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012, NI 43-101, Internal Exploration Standard

attributes.name: hole_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the drill hole. Planned holes are scheduled but not started; in-progress holes are actively being drilled; completed holes have reached target depth and been logged; abandoned holes were terminated early due to technical issues; suspended holes are temporarily halted; surveyed holes have had final downhole survey completed.

attributes.name: logged_date
attributes.description: The date the geological logging of the drill hole was completed. Used for workflow tracking and data currency assessment.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this drill hole record was last modified in the system. Used for data currency assessment, change tracking, and audit trail.

attributes.name: planned_azimuth
attributes.description: The planned horizontal direction of the drill hole at the collar, measured in degrees clockwise from grid north (0-360). Azimuth defines the compass bearing of the hole trajectory.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Drilling Standard

attributes.name: planned_depth
attributes.description: The planned total depth of the drill hole measured along the hole trajectory from collar to end-of-hole, measured in meters. Defines the target depth for the drilling contractor.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Drilling Contract Standard

attributes.name: planned_dip
attributes.description: The planned vertical angle of the drill hole at the collar, measured in degrees from horizontal. Positive values indicate downward inclination; negative values indicate upward inclination. A vertical hole has a dip of -90 degrees.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Drilling Standard

attributes.name: pre_collar_depth
attributes.description: The depth of pre-collar drilling (typically RC or aircore) completed before switching to diamond core drilling, measured in meters. Used in two-stage drilling programs to reduce diamond drilling costs through overburden.

attributes.name: qaqc_status
attributes.description: The overall quality assurance and quality control status for this drill hole, based on review of sampling procedures, assay QAQC results, survey accuracy, and logging completeness. Passed holes are suitable for resource estimation; failed holes require remediation or exclusion.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Internal QAQC Standard

attributes.name: recovery_percentage
attributes.description: The average percentage of core recovered relative to the drilled interval, applicable to diamond core drilling. High recovery (>95%) indicates competent ground and good drilling practice; low recovery may indicate fractured ground, voids, or drilling issues. Critical for resource confidence classification.

attributes.name: sample_interval
attributes.description: The standard length interval used for sampling this drill hole, measured in meters. Typically 1m for RC drilling and variable (0.5-1.5m) for diamond core based on geological contacts. Used for sample planning and assay result interpretation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Sampling Standard

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date drilling operations commenced for this hole. Used for program scheduling, contractor performance tracking, and cost allocation.

attributes.name: survey_method
attributes.description: The method used to survey the drill hole trajectory. Gyroscopic surveys are most accurate and unaffected by magnetic interference; magnetic surveys are cost-effective but affected by magnetic ore bodies; electronic multi-shot provides continuous trajectory; differential GPS and total station are used for collar positioning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: gyroscopic|magnetic|electronic_multi_shot|single_shot|differential_gps|total_station|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, NI 43-101, Survey Standard

attributes.name: target_geology
attributes.description: Free-text description of the geological target or formation being intersected by this drill hole. Includes target lithology, structure, or mineralization style. Used for geological interpretation and targeting review.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Table 1 Section 1, Internal Geology Standard

products.name: drill_program
products.description: Defines a planned and executed drilling campaign associated with a prospect or resource area. Captures program name, target commodity, program type (scout, infill, step-out, resource definition), planned versus actual hole count, planned versus actual metreage, program start and end dates, approved budget (CAPEX/OPEX), actual expenditure, program objectives, and sign-off status. Links to the exploration licence and prospect. Enables LOM drilling program tracking and JORC-compliant resource update planning.

attributes.name: drill_program_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the drilling program. Primary key for the drill program entity.

attributes.name: capex_budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_budget. Business justification: Drill programs are capital projects requiring budget approval and tracking. Finance links drill program expenditure to approved capex budgets for capital expenditure control and variance reporting.

attributes.name: competent_person_id
attributes.description: FK to exploration.competent_person

attributes.name: contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.contract. Business justification: Drilling programs operate under framework agreements or master service agreements. Links program to procurement contract for pricing verification, terms compliance, scope management, and contract perf

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Drill programs incur direct costs posted to a cost centre for monthly exploration cost reporting and budget variance analysis. Standard mining ERP practice assigns a cost centre to each drill program

attributes.name: drill_rig_asset_class_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drill Rig Asset Class Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to equipment.asset_class. Business justification: Drill programs specify required rig class (RC, diamond core, RAB) before a specific asset is assigned. This drives fleet procurement, CAPEX budgeting, and contractor tendering. A Mining planner would

attributes.name: drilling_contractor_procurement_vendor_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Drilling Contractor Procurement Vendor Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.procurement_vendor. Mining procurement requires all contractors to exist in the vendor

Business justification: Drilling programs must reference site emergency response plans (medical evacuation, spill response, rig fire). Operational requirement for contractor mobilization and safety induction. Plan ID include

attributes.name: environmental_permit_id

attributes.name: expenditure_commitment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.expenditure_commitment. Business justification: Drill programs are the primary mechanism for satisfying tenement minimum expenditure commitments. Tenement managers track which drill programs contribute to which commitment obligations for statutory

attributes.name: mine_site_id

attributes.name: opex_budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.opex_budget. Business justification: Drill programs have operational expenditure components (consumables, labor, contractor costs). Finance links drill programs to opex budgets for operating cost control and AISC calculation.

attributes.name: profit_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_centre. Business justification: Drill programs are assigned to profit centres for commodity segment reporting and exploration accounting under IFRS 6. Mining finance requires profit centre on drill programs to correctly classify exp

attributes.name: prospect_id

attributes.name: target_commodity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: Drill programs are designed to test commodity-specific targets - required for budget allocation, statutory expenditure reporting, and drilling contractor selection (e.g., RC vs diamond core). Normaliz

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Drill programs are executed under specific tenement rights. Statutory minimum expenditure reporting requires drill program metreage and spend to be attributed directly to a tenement — regulators asses

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Drill programs are capital/opex projects tracked against WBS elements in SAP for JORC expenditure compliance and cost control reporting. Mining finance teams require WBS assignment on every drill prog

attributes.name: actual_expenditure_amount
attributes.description: Total actual expenditure incurred for the drilling program to date. Used for budget variance analysis and cost control.
attributes.references: IFRS 6 Exploration and Evaluation of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: actual_hole_count
attributes.description: Total number of drill holes actually completed as part of this program. Used for program performance tracking and variance analysis.

attributes.name: actual_metreage
attributes.description: Total actual drilling metreage (in metres) completed for the program. Used for cost reconciliation and performance tracking against plan.

attributes.name: approved_budget_amount
attributes.description: Total approved budget for the drilling program in the reporting currency. Includes drilling, assay, geological support, and mobilization costs.
attributes.references: IFRS 6 Exploration and Evaluation of Mineral Resources

attributes.name: budget_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the approved budget and actual expenditure amounts (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the drill program record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: drilling_method
attributes.description: Primary drilling technique employed in the program: diamond core (DD), reverse circulation (RC), rotary air blast (RAB), percussion, or sonic drilling. Determines sample quality and cost profile.

attributes.name: expenditure_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the drilling program expenditure as Capital Expenditure (CAPEX), Operating Expenditure (OPEX), or mixed. Critical for financial reporting and tax treatment under IFRS 6.

attributes.name: hse_incident_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Incident Count
attributes.description: Total number of recordable Health, Safety, and Environment incidents that occurred during the execution of the drilling program. Used for safety performance tracking and LTIFR/TRIFR calculation.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether this drill program record is currently active and valid for operational and reporting purposes. Supports soft-delete and historical record management.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the drill program record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data governance.

attributes.name: planned_hole_count
attributes.description: Total number of drill holes planned for this program as per the approved drilling plan.

attributes.name: planned_metreage
attributes.description: Total planned drilling metreage (in metres) for the program as per the approved drilling plan. Critical for budget estimation and contractor scoping.

attributes.name: program_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or code assigned to the drilling program for external reference and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: program_end_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual date when drilling operations concluded for this program. Used for program duration tracking and contractor demobilization planning.

attributes.name: program_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the drilling program identifying the campaign, location, or strategic objective.

attributes.name: program_objective
attributes.description: Detailed description of the strategic and technical objectives of the drilling program, including target resource category upgrade, geological model validation, or feasibility study support.

attributes.name: program_start_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual date when drilling operations commenced for this program. Critical for Life of Mine (LOM) planning and resource update scheduling.

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the drilling program: planned (design phase), approved (budget authorized), active (drilling underway), suspended (temporarily halted), completed (all holes drilled and signed off), or cancelled (terminated before completion).

attributes.name: program_type
attributes.description: Classification of the drilling program based on its strategic purpose: scout (initial exploration), infill (increasing resource confidence), step-out (extending known mineralization), resource definition (JORC/NI 43-101 compliance), geotechnical (engineering studies), or condemnation (proving absence of mineralization).

attributes.name: qaqc_protocol_applied
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QAQC) Protocol Applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal QAQC protocol (including certified reference materials, blanks, and duplicates) was applied during the drilling program to ensure sample integrity and assay reliability.

attributes.name: rehabilitation_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether site rehabilitation (drill pad restoration, collar capping, and environmental remediation) has been completed following the conclusion of the drilling program.
attributes.references: ISO 14001, Mine Closure and Rehabilitation Standard

attributes.name: rehabilitation_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when site rehabilitation activities were completed and the drill site was returned to its pre-disturbance condition or approved final land use.
attributes.references: ISO 14001, Mine Closure and Rehabilitation Standard

attributes.name: sign_off_date
attributes.description: Date when the Competent Person formally approved the drilling program results for inclusion in resource and reserve reporting.

attributes.name: sign_off_status
attributes.description: Approval status of the drilling program results by the Competent Person: pending (awaiting review), in_review (under technical review), approved (signed off for resource update), or rejected (requires additional work).

attributes.name: target_resource_category
attributes.description: JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC resource classification category that the drilling program aims to achieve or upgrade: inferred (lowest confidence), indicated (moderate confidence), or measured (highest confidence).

products.name: drill_hole_survey
products.description: Downhole survey measurements capturing the deviation of a drill hole from its planned trajectory at regular depth intervals. Records hole ID, survey depth, measured azimuth, measured dip, survey instrument type (gyroscope, magnetic, multi-shot), survey date, and surveyor. Essential for accurate 3D spatial positioning of assay intervals and geological logging data used in resource estimation and Geovia GEMS block model construction.

attributes.name: drill_hole_survey_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the drill hole survey measurement record.

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent drill hole for which this survey measurement was taken.

attributes.name: survey_instrument_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to equipment.asset. Business justification: Downhole survey instruments (gyroscopes, magnetic tools) are tracked as equipment assets requiring calibration and maintenance records. Linking drill_hole_survey to the instrument asset enables calibr

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.procurement_vendor. Business justification: Downhole directional surveys are performed by specialist survey contractors who are registered vendors. Mining operations require vendor traceability for instrument calibration records, insurance comp

attributes.name: calculated_easting
attributes.description: Calculated easting coordinate at this survey depth based on collar position, azimuth, and dip measurements.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Geological Modeling - Spatial Calculations

attributes.name: calculated_elevation
attributes.description: Calculated elevation (reduced level) at this survey depth based on collar elevation and dip measurements.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Geological Modeling - Spatial Calculations

attributes.name: calculated_northing
attributes.description: Calculated northing coordinate at this survey depth based on collar position, azimuth, and dip measurements.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Geological Modeling - Spatial Calculations

attributes.name: calibration_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent calibration of the survey instrument prior to this measurement.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments or notes regarding this survey measurement, including any anomalies, instrument issues, or special conditions.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Spatial reference system or coordinate system used for azimuth and spatial calculations (e.g., WGS84, local mine grid, UTM zone).

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Source system or database from which this survey measurement was imported (e.g., Hexagon MinePlan, Geovia GEMS, contractor database).

attributes.name: deviation_from_planned
attributes.description: Calculated horizontal deviation distance from the planned drill hole trajectory at this survey depth, measured in meters.

attributes.name: magnetic_declination
attributes.description: Magnetic declination correction applied to convert magnetic azimuth to true azimuth at the survey location and date. Positive values indicate eastward declination.
attributes.references: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information - Magnetic Declination

attributes.name: magnetic_field_strength
attributes.description: Magnetic field strength measured at the survey point in nanoTesla. High magnetic interference may affect magnetic survey instrument accuracy.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: measured_azimuth
attributes.description: Horizontal angle of the drill hole at this survey point, measured in degrees clockwise from true north (0-360).
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: measured_dip
attributes.description: Vertical angle of the drill hole at this survey point, measured in degrees from horizontal. Negative values indicate downward inclination.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this survey measurement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this survey measurement record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: survey_date
attributes.description: Date on which the downhole survey measurement was taken.

attributes.name: survey_depth
attributes.description: Depth down the hole at which this survey measurement was taken, measured in meters from the collar.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Drilling and Sampling Standards

attributes.name: survey_instrument_type
attributes.description: Type of downhole survey instrument used to capture this measurement. Gyroscope instruments are preferred for accuracy in magnetic environments.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: survey_method
attributes.description: Method by which the survey was conducted: end of hole survey, during drilling at intervals, post-drilling, or continuous measurement.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: survey_quality_code
attributes.description: Quality assessment code indicating the reliability and verification status of this survey measurement.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: survey_run_number
attributes.description: Sequential number identifying the survey run or trip down the hole. Multiple runs may be performed for verification.

attributes.name: survey_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of this survey measurement record in the data validation and approval process.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: temperature_at_survey
attributes.description: Temperature recorded at the survey depth during measurement, in degrees Celsius. Temperature can affect instrument accuracy.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: validated_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the geologist or data manager who validated and approved this survey measurement.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: validation_date
attributes.description: Date on which this survey measurement was validated and approved for use in resource estimation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 - Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data

products.name: geological_log
products.description: Detailed geological logging records for each drill hole interval during exploration and resource definition drilling. Captures lithology, rock type, alteration type and intensity, mineralisation style, structural features, RQD (Rock Quality Designation), recovery percentage, colour, grain size, weathering, oxidation state, and geologist identifier. Logged at defined depth intervals (from-to) per drill hole. Scoped to exploration-phase drilling — production-phase grade control logging is owned by the geology domain. Forms the primary geological dataset for resource estimation and JORC Table 1 Section 1 disclosures.

attributes.name: geological_log_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the geological log record. Primary key for the geological log entity. Inferred role: EVENT_LOG (append-only geological observations per drill hole interval).

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the drill hole from which this geological log was recorded. Links to the drill hole collar and survey data. Represents the EVENT_SOURCE_REFERENCE for this log entry.

attributes.name: hazard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.hazard. Business justification: Geological logs identify hazardous lithologies (asbestos-bearing formations, acid-generating rock, naturally occurring radioactive material). Mining HSE and environmental regulations require geologist

attributes.name: alteration_intensity
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the intensity or degree of alteration observed: none, weak, moderate, strong, or pervasive. Used in conjunction with alteration_type for resource modeling.

attributes.name: alteration_type
attributes.description: Type of hydrothermal or weathering alteration observed in the interval (e.g., silicification, chloritisation, sericitisation, hematisation). Critical for understanding mineralization processes and JORC Table 1 Section 1 reporting.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 1; Alteration Classification Standards

attributes.name: colour
attributes.description: Primary colour of the rock observed in the interval (e.g., grey, red, green, black, white). May indicate oxidation state, alteration, or lithology.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments and observations recorded by the geologist during logging. May include additional details not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: core_condition
attributes.description: Overall condition of the drill core: excellent, good, fair, poor, or very_poor. Reflects core integrity and quality for geological interpretation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this geological log record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for data lineage and JORC compliance.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Source of the geological log data: field_logging (original logging at drill site), re_logging (subsequent re-interpretation), or historical_import (legacy data migration).

attributes.name: depth_from
attributes.description: Starting depth of the logged interval in meters below surface or collar. Used to define the from-to interval for geological observations.

attributes.name: depth_to
attributes.description: Ending depth of the logged interval in meters below surface or collar. Used to define the from-to interval for geological observations.

attributes.name: grain_size
attributes.description: Classification of the grain size of the rock: very_fine, fine, medium, coarse, or very_coarse. Relevant for sedimentary and some igneous rocks.

attributes.name: hardness
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of rock hardness: very_soft, soft, medium, hard, or very_hard. Relevant for drilling performance and geotechnical assessment.

attributes.name: interval_length
attributes.description: Length of the logged interval in meters, calculated as depth_to minus depth_from. Represents the sample or observation interval.

attributes.name: lithology_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing the primary rock type observed in this interval (e.g., BIF for Banded Iron Formation, GRN for Granite, SHL for Shale). Follows site-specific or regional lithology coding standards.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 1; Site Geological Standards

attributes.name: lithology_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the rock type, including texture, grain size, composition, and any distinguishing features observed by the geologist.

attributes.name: logging_date
attributes.description: Date when the geological logging was performed. Represents the EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this observation. Critical for data lineage and JORC Table 1 Section 1 reporting.

attributes.name: logging_method
attributes.description: Method used to perform the geological logging: visual (traditional manual logging), digital (tablet-based logging), or photographic (image-based logging with subsequent interpretation).
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 1; Internal Logging Standards

attributes.name: mineralisation_intensity
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the intensity or abundance of visible mineralization: none, trace, minor, moderate, or strong. Used for preliminary grade estimation and targeting.

attributes.name: mineralisation_style
attributes.description: Description of the style and form of mineralization observed (e.g., disseminated, vein-hosted, massive sulfide, replacement, stockwork). Critical for understanding ore body geometry and JORC reporting.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 1; NI 43-101; SAMREC

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this geological log record was last modified. Part of audit trail for data lineage and change tracking.

attributes.name: oxidation_state
attributes.description: Oxidation state of the mineralization: oxide (fully oxidized), transitional (partially oxidized), or fresh_sulfide (unoxidized). Critical for metallurgical processing and resource classification.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 1; Metallurgical Classification Standards

attributes.name: qaqc_status
attributes.description: Quality control status of the geological log record: pending (awaiting review), approved (validated and accepted), rejected (failed QC checks), or under_review (currently being reviewed). Critical for JORC Table 1 Section 1 data quality reporting.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 1; Internal QA/QC Standards

attributes.name: recovery_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of core recovered from the drilled interval, calculated as recovered core length divided by drilled interval length. Critical quality indicator for drill hole data and JORC Table 1 Section 1 reporting.

attributes.name: rock_type
attributes.description: High-level classification of the rock type into major geological categories: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic, or unconsolidated material.

attributes.name: rqd_percent
attributes.description: Rock Quality Designation expressed as a percentage, calculated as the sum of core pieces greater than 10cm divided by the interval length. Standard geotechnical measure of rock mass quality ranging from 0 to 100 percent.
attributes.references: ISRM Standards; JORC Code Table 1 Section 1

attributes.name: sample_collected_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether a physical sample was collected from this interval for assay analysis. True if sample was collected, False otherwise.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 1; Laboratory Sample Management

attributes.name: structure_orientation
attributes.description: Orientation of structural features recorded as dip direction and dip angle (e.g., 045/60 meaning dipping 60 degrees towards 045 azimuth). Critical for structural modeling and geotechnical assessment.

attributes.name: structure_type
attributes.description: Type of structural feature observed in the interval (e.g., fault, shear zone, joint, fracture, foliation, bedding). Important for understanding ore controls and geotechnical properties.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 1; Structural Geology Standards

attributes.name: texture
attributes.description: Description of the rock texture (e.g., massive, foliated, banded, brecciated, porphyritic). Provides information on rock formation and deformation history.

attributes.name: vein_type
attributes.description: Description of vein mineralogy and characteristics (e.g., quartz vein, calcite vein, sulfide vein). Critical for understanding mineralization style and ore genesis.

attributes.name: veining_percent
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of the interval occupied by veins. Important for understanding mineralization distribution and structural controls.

attributes.name: weathering_degree
attributes.description: Degree of weathering observed in the rock: fresh, slightly_weathered, moderately_weathered, highly_weathered, or completely_weathered. Important for understanding near-surface ore characteristics and geotechnical properties.
attributes.references: Weathering Classification Standards; JORC Code Table 1 Section 1

products.name: exploration_sample
products.description: Master record for every physical sample collected during exploration activities including drill core (half-core, quarter-core), RC chips, channel samples, soil samples, rock chips, and stream sediment samples. Captures sample ID, sample type, collection method, drill hole reference, from-to depth interval, sample weight, sample length, dispatch batch number, dispatch date to laboratory, chain of custody status, QA/QC type (routine, duplicate, blank, standard, replicate), and preparation instructions. The SSOT for sample identity and collection metadata in the exploration domain; analytical results (assays) are owned by the laboratory domain and linked back via sample ID foreign key.

attributes.name: exploration_sample_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the exploration sample record. Primary key for the sample entity.

attributes.name: collection_equipment_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to equipment.asset. Business justification: Exploration samples (soil, rock chip, channel) are collected using specific equipment (augers, excavators, portable drills). Tracking collection equipment supports QA/QC protocols, method validation,

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.description: Reference to the drill hole from which this sample was collected. Null for non-drill samples such as soil, rock chip, or stream sediment samples.

attributes.name: geological_log_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.geological_log. Business justification: An exploration sample collected from a drill core interval is directly associated with the geological log entry for that interval. geological_log has sample_collected_flag indicating a sample was take

attributes.name: hazard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.hazard. Business justification: Exploration samples from hazardous materials (radioactive minerals, asbestos, acid-generating rock) must reference the relevant hazard for safe handling, storage, and disposal. Mining HSE regulations

attributes.name: parent_sample_exploration_sample_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original sample from which this sample was derived (e.g., for duplicates, replicates, or sub-samples). Null for primary field samples.

attributes.name: prospect_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.prospect. Business justification: Exploration samples are collected from specific prospects. Currently sample stores prospect_code as a denormalized string identifier. Adding prospect_id FK to the prospect master table normalizes this

attributes.name: survey_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.survey. Business justification: Surface samples (soil, rock chip, stream sediment, water) collected during a geochemical or geophysical survey program should reference the survey they belong to. exploration_sample already has drill_

attributes.name: target_saleable_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.saleable_product. Business justification: Exploration samples in feasibility-stage projects are tested against target product specifications (e.g., lump vs fines iron ore, concentrate grade) - critical for metallurgical testwork, product qual

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: exploration_sample carries a plain 'tenement_code' attribute — a denormalized reference to tenement.statutory_identifier. Chain-of-custody documentation and statutory sample reporting require samples

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Assay laboratories are vendors providing analytical services. Links samples to vendor master for lab performance tracking, cost analysis, quality correlation, turnaround time monitoring, and contract

attributes.name: warehouse_location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.warehouse_location. Business justification: Exploration samples are physically stored in site warehouses or cool rooms before dispatch to laboratories. Linking to warehouse_location enables chain-of-custody tracking, storage condition complianc

attributes.name: alteration_code
attributes.description: Code representing the type and intensity of hydrothermal or weathering alteration observed in the sample. Important for understanding mineralization controls.

attributes.name: analytical_method
attributes.description: Requested analytical technique or method suite for this sample (e.g., fire assay, ICP-MS, XRF). Determines which elements or compounds will be analyzed and detection limits.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Sample Preparation and Analysis

attributes.name: chain_of_custody_status
attributes.description: Current physical location or custody status of the sample. Critical for sample tracking, security, and audit compliance.

attributes.name: collection_date
attributes.description: Date when the sample was physically collected from the field or drill site. Critical for chain of custody and temporal analysis of exploration programs.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: collection_method
attributes.description: The technique or equipment used to collect the sample from the field. Critical for understanding sample quality, representativeness, and potential biases.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Spatial reference system used for the sample location coordinates (e.g., WGS84 UTM Zone 50S, GDA94 MGA Zone 51). Critical for accurate spatial integration.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Location of Data Points

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this sample record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: dispatch_batch_number
attributes.description: Identifier for the batch or shipment in which this sample was sent to the laboratory. Used for tracking, logistics, and grouping samples for analysis.

attributes.name: dispatch_date
attributes.description: Date when the sample was dispatched from the field or core facility to the analytical laboratory. Part of chain of custody documentation.

attributes.name: easting_m
attributes.description: Easting coordinate of the sample collection point in meters, typically in a projected coordinate system (e.g., UTM). Used for spatial analysis and resource modeling.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Location of Data Points

attributes.name: elevation_m
attributes.description: Elevation of the sample collection point in meters above mean sea level. Used for 3D spatial modeling and geological interpretation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Location of Data Points

attributes.name: from_depth_m
attributes.description: Starting depth in meters of the sample interval measured from drill hole collar. Null for surface samples. Used with to_depth_m to define the sample interval.

attributes.name: geologist_comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for geologist observations, notes, or interpretations recorded during sample collection or logging. Captures qualitative information not represented in coded fields.

attributes.name: is_composite
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this sample is a composite created by combining multiple individual samples. Composites are used for resource estimation and grade control.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this sample record was last updated in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: length_m
attributes.description: Physical length of the sample interval in meters. For drill samples, typically calculated as to_depth_m minus from_depth_m. Critical for understanding sample support and compositing.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: lithology_code
attributes.description: Code representing the rock type or geological unit observed at the sample interval. Used for geological modeling and domain definition.

attributes.name: mineralization_code
attributes.description: Code representing the style, type, or intensity of mineralization observed in the sample. Used for targeting and geological interpretation.

attributes.name: northing_m
attributes.description: Northing coordinate of the sample collection point in meters, typically in a projected coordinate system (e.g., UTM). Used for spatial analysis and resource modeling.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Location of Data Points

attributes.name: preparation_instructions
attributes.description: Specific instructions for laboratory sample preparation including crushing, grinding, splitting, and sub-sampling protocols. May reference standard preparation codes or custom procedures.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Sample Preparation and Analysis

attributes.name: qaqc_reference_material
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QAQC) Reference Material
attributes.description: Identifier of the certified reference material (CRM) or standard used for this QAQC sample. Null for routine samples. Used to validate laboratory accuracy.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Quality of Assay Data and Laboratory Tests

attributes.name: qaqc_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sample for quality assurance and quality control purposes. Routine samples are normal field samples; duplicates, blanks, standards, and replicates are control samples inserted to monitor analytical accuracy and precision.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Quality of Assay Data and Laboratory Tests

attributes.name: recovery_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of core or sample material recovered relative to the drilled or sampled interval. Low recovery may indicate sample quality issues or geological conditions such as voids or fracturing.

attributes.name: sample_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique sample identifier assigned during collection. Used for laboratory tracking, chain of custody, and cross-referencing with assay results. Typically follows site-specific numbering conventions.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: sample_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sample in the exploration workflow. Tracks progression from field collection through laboratory analysis to final data integration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: collected|dispatched|at_laboratory|prepared|assayed|completed|cancelled — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: sample_type
attributes.description: Classification of the physical sample based on collection method and material form. Determines handling, preparation, and analytical protocols. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: drill_core_half|drill_core_quarter|rc_chips|channel|soil|rock_chip|stream_sediment — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 1 - Sampling Techniques and Data

attributes.name: to_depth_m
attributes.description: Ending depth in meters of the sample interval measured from drill hole collar. Null for surface samples. Used with from_depth_m to define the sample interval.

products.name: resource_estimation_input
products.description: This association product represents the Role relationship between resource_estimate and drill_hole. It captures the explicit inclusion of a drill hole in a specific mineral resource estimate, recording the geologist's decision to include or exclude the hole, the statistical weight assigned, the number of assay intervals used, and whether samples were composited. Each record links one resource_estimate to one drill_hole with attributes that exist only in the context of this estimation relationship. This is the authoritative record for regulatory audit of resource estimation inputs under JORC 2012, NI 43-101, and SAMREC.. Existence Justification: In mining resource estimation, geologists explicitly manage which drill holes are included in each resource estimate — a drill hole can contribute data to multiple resource estimates (e.g., an initial estimate, an updated estimate, and a final JORC estimate for the same deposit), and a resource estimate draws on many drill holes. This is an actively managed operational relationship: geologists create, update, and delete inclusion records as estimates are revised, tracking which holes were used, how they were composited, and what weight they carried. The business concept is well-recognised as the 'drill hole database' or 'resource estimation input set' and is subject to regulatory audit under JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC.

attributes.name: resource_estimation_input_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Resource Estimation Input - Resource Estimation Input Id
attributes.description: Primary key for the resource_estimation_input association

attributes.name: drill_hole_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Resource Estimation Input - Drill Hole Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the drill hole whose assay data is being included or excluded from the resource estimate.

attributes.name: resource_estimate_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Resource Estimation Input - Resource Estimate Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the mineral resource estimate that this drill hole input record belongs to.

attributes.name: composite_sample_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the assay samples from this drill hole were composited (e.g., regularised to 2m composites) before being used in the estimation. Compositing decisions are per-hole per-estimate and belong to this association.

attributes.name: contribution_weight
attributes.description: The statistical weight assigned to this drill hole within the resource estimation algorithm (e.g., kriging weight, IDW distance-based weight). Belongs to the association because the same hole may carry different weights in different estimates.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this drill hole inclusion record was first created, supporting audit trail requirements under JORC 2012 and NI 43-101 for resource estimation dataset provenance.

attributes.name: domain_code
attributes.description: The mineralisation domain or estimation domain within which this drill hole's data was used. A single hole may intersect multiple domains; this attribute records which domain context applies for this estimate inclusion record.

attributes.name: drill_hole_count
attributes.description: Total number of drill holes used as input data for this resource estimate. [Moved from resource_estimate: This INT aggregate on resource_estimate is derivable by COUNT(*) WHERE included_flag = TRUE on this association table. Storing it as a denormalised count on the estimate creates a maintenance burden and risks inconsistency. It should be removed from resource_estimate and computed from this association product.]

attributes.name: exclusion_reason
attributes.description: Free-text reason why this drill hole was excluded from the resource estimate (e.g., insufficient depth, poor core recovery, outside domain boundary, superseded by closer hole). Only populated when included_flag is FALSE. Required for JORC Table 1 audit compliance.

attributes.name: included_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this drill hole was included (TRUE) or explicitly excluded (FALSE) from the resource estimate. Excluded holes are still recorded to provide a complete audit trail of the estimation dataset decision.

attributes.name: interval_count_used
attributes.description: The number of assay intervals (downhole sample intervals) from this drill hole that were used as input data in the resource estimate. A hole may have 200 intervals but only 150 within the mineralised domain used for estimation.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this drill hole inclusion record was last modified, supporting change tracking for regulatory compliance and estimate revision history.

products.name: drill_target
products.description: This association product represents the DrillTarget — the formal business entity in mineral exploration that links a specific survey (and its anomaly) to a drill program. It captures the targeting rationale, anomaly reference, priority ranking, and follow-up type that justify the inclusion of a survey-derived anomaly in a drill program. Each record documents one survey-to-program targeting decision, enabling traceability from survey anomaly through to drill hole execution and resource update. Supports JORC-compliant documentation of exploration targeting workflows.. Existence Justification: In mineral exploration, surveys (geophysical and geochemical) generate anomalies and drill targets that are formally documented and then grouped into drill programs. A single survey can generate targets that feed into multiple drill programs (e.g., a regional airborne magnetics survey informs both a scout program and a later resource definition program), and a single drill program is typically justified by and references multiple surveys (e.g., IP survey + soil geochemistry + rock chip program all pointing to the same target zone). Exploration geologists actively manage this linkage as a 'drill target' — a recognised business entity that records which survey anomaly generated which drill target, its priority, and the rationale for inclusion in a program.

attributes.name: drill_target_id
attributes.description: Primary key for the drill_target association

attributes.name: drill_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking this drill target to the drill program it has been assigned to or is being considered for.

attributes.name: survey_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking this drill target to the survey whose anomaly or result generated this target.

attributes.name: anomaly_reference
attributes.description: Identifier or label for the specific anomaly within the survey that generated this drill target (e.g., anomaly ID, grid reference, or named anomaly). Belongs to the relationship because a single survey may contain many anomalies, only some of which are linked to a given program.

attributes.name: drill_targets_generated
attributes.description: Number of drill targets prioritized from this survey for inclusion in future drilling programs. Subset of total anomalies that pass economic and technical filters. [Moved from survey: drill_targets_generated on survey is a derived count of how many drill targets were generated from that survey. With the drill_target association table in place, this count is derivable via COUNT(drill_target_id) WHERE survey_id = X. Storing it as a denormalised integer on the survey creates a maintenance burden and risks inconsistency. It should be removed from survey and computed from the association.]

attributes.name: follow_up_type

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Ranked priority of this drill target within the drill program (e.g., 1 = highest priority). Priority is assigned in the context of a specific program and cannot reside on either the survey or the drill program alone.

attributes.name: target_generated_date
attributes.description: Date on which this drill target was formally created from the survey interpretation and added to the targeting register. Records the point in time when the exploration team recognised the anomaly as a drill-worthy target.

products.name: production_drillhole
products.description: Master register of all drillholes (exploration, resource definition, grade control, geotechnical, and hydrogeological) across all projects and mine sites. Records collar location (easting, northing, RL), azimuth, dip, total depth, hole type (RC, diamond, RAB, AC), drilling contractor, rig identifier, purpose, status, and JORC reporting category. The SSOT for drillhole identity — geology domain owns the master record; exploration domain references via FK for program planning. Integrates with Geovia GEMS and LabWare LIMS for assay linkage.
products.reference: JORC Code 2012 – Section 1 Sampling Techniques and Data
