attributes.name: environmental_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.environmental_permit. Business justification: Pit designs must comply with permitted disturbance footprint and depth limits. Required for permit compliance verification and regulatory submissions showing design is within approved boundaries.

attributes.name: functional_location_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent pit or open-cut entity that this design belongs to. A single pit may have multiple design revisions or pushback stages over its life.

attributes.name: geological_domain_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.geological_domain. Business justification: Pit designs respect geological domain boundaries for grade control and geotechnical stability. Required for optimizing pit shells, managing dilution, and ensuring design aligns with geological structu

attributes.name: heritage_clearance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.heritage_clearance. Business justification: Pit design approval requires confirming the pit footprint is covered by a valid heritage clearance. Regulatory authorities require heritage clearance status to be demonstrated before pit design approv

attributes.name: lom_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Life of Mine (LOM) plan under which this pit design was created or is currently active. Enables traceability of design decisions to the governing LOM schedule.

attributes.name: mine_site_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.mine_site. Business justification: pit_design has mine_site_code (STRING) but no FK to mine_site table. Adding mine_site_id FK normalizes site reference and removes redundant code column. The mine_site table contains site_code.

attributes.name: orebody_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.orebody. Business justification: Pit designs target specific orebodies for extraction. Essential for mine planning, resource allocation, and regulatory reporting. Domain experts expect pit designs to reference their target orebody.

attributes.name: pit_or_level_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.pit_or_level. Business justification: A pit design is created for a specific pit or level. This FK links the pit design master record to the spatial pit/level entity it defines, enabling navigation from design to operational pit context.

attributes.name: prospect_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.prospect. Business justification: Pit designs are developed for specific exploration prospects that have been converted to mineable resources. Mine planning teams reference the original prospect to validate design assumptions, resourc

attributes.name: rehabilitation_provision_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.rehabilitation_provision. Business justification: Pit design geometry (depth, area, slope angles) directly drives rehabilitation cost estimates and closure liability provisions under IFRS/AASB 137. Mine closure engineers use pit design parameters to

attributes.name: resource_estimate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.resource_estimate. Business justification: Pit shell optimisation (Whittle/Deswik) is run against a specific resource estimate version. Reserve reporting audit trails and pit design sign-off require a traceable FK to the resource estimate used

attributes.name: surface_right_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.surface_right. Business justification: Pit designs require surface rights over the land to be disturbed. The design approval process must confirm surface rights are in place before the pit design can be approved and construction commenced.

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Pit designs must be spatially validated against tenement boundaries before regulatory approval. Mining engineers verify designs remain within licensed areas for Programme of Work submissions and envir

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Pit designs are developed under capital projects tracked via WBS elements for design capex, engineering cost control, and project cost tracking. Capital project link for open-pit mining.

attributes.name: wireframe_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.wireframe. Business justification: Pit designs use orebody wireframes as geometric constraints for optimization. Required for pit shell generation, ensuring designs respect geological boundaries, and volume calculations.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the engineering authority (e.g., Chief Mine Planner, Geotechnical Manager) who formally approved this pit design for use in mine planning and scheduling.

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which the pit design was formally approved by the responsible engineering authority for use in mine planning and scheduling. Null if not yet approved.

attributes.name: bench_height_m
attributes.description: The vertical height of each mining bench in metres. Determines the drilling and blasting pattern, equipment selection, and ore/waste delineation resolution. Typically 5–15 m for large open-cut operations.

attributes.name: berm_width_m
attributes.description: The width of catch berms (safety benches) in metres between inter-ramp slope segments. Berms are designed to catch falling material and provide geotechnical stability. Minimum berm width is governed by geotechnical design criteria.

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: The spatial coordinate reference system (CRS) used for the pit design geometry (e.g., 'GDA2020 / MGA Zone 51', 'WGS84 UTM Zone 50S'). Required for GIS integration and spatial accuracy of the pit shell.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan; Geovia GEMS; GIS Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pit design record was first created in the lakehouse data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking in the silver layer.
attributes.references: IFRS 6; ISO 14001; GRI Mining and Metals Sector Supplement

attributes.name: cutoff_grade
attributes.description: The minimum economic grade (concentration of target mineral) used to classify material as ore versus waste within this pit design. Expressed in the commodity-appropriate unit (e.g., % Fe for iron ore, % Cu for copper, g/t Au for gold). Drives ore/waste classification in the block model.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan; Geovia GEMS; JORC Code 2012; CIM Standards; SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: cutoff_grade_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the cut-off grade value (e.g., 'pct' for percentage Fe/Cu, 'g_per_t' for grams per tonne Au/Ag, 'ppm' for parts per million). Required to correctly interpret the cutoff_grade field.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; CIM Standards; SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: design_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this pit design within the mine planning system (e.g., PIT-NW-001-R3). Used as the business-facing reference across engineering, scheduling, and LOM planning documents.

attributes.name: design_engineer
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the mine planning or geotechnical engineer responsible for authoring this pit design revision. Used for accountability and design review traceability.

attributes.name: design_file_reference
attributes.description: File path or document management system reference to the source design file (e.g., DXF, DWG, or MinePlan project file) containing the pit shell geometry. Enables engineers to retrieve the authoritative spatial data.

attributes.name: design_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the pit design (e.g., 'North-West Pit Stage 3 Pushback'). Used in reports, LOM schedules, and stakeholder communications.

attributes.name: design_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for engineering notes, assumptions, constraints, or change rationale associated with this pit design revision. Captures context not represented in structured fields.

attributes.name: design_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pit design record. 'draft' indicates work-in-progress; 'under_review' means submitted for engineering or geotechnical review; 'approved' is the authorised design for mine planning; 'superseded' means replaced by a newer revision; 'archived' is retained for historical reference only.

attributes.name: design_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pit design indicating its engineering purpose. 'ultimate_pit' is the final planned pit extent; 'pushback' or 'cutback' represents an incremental mining stage; 'stage' is a scheduled mining increment; 'interim' is a temporary design used for short-term planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ultimate_pit|pushback|stage|cutback|interim|exploration — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this pit design is considered the active and authoritative design for mine planning purposes. Supports temporal versioning of pit designs across LOM schedule periods.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this pit design ceases to be the active authoritative design, typically when superseded by a new revision. Null for the currently active design.

attributes.name: face_angle_deg
attributes.description: The bench face angle in degrees, representing the angle of the individual bench face from horizontal. Determined by rock mass strength and blasting parameters. Typically 65°–80° for competent rock.

attributes.name: geotechnical_domain
attributes.description: The geotechnical domain or zone classification applied to this pit design, reflecting the rock mass characterisation used to determine slope angle parameters. Sourced from the geotechnical model underpinning the design.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan; Geovia GEMS; JORC Code 2012

attributes.name: hydrogeology_considered
attributes.description: Indicates whether hydrogeological conditions (groundwater, dewatering requirements) were explicitly incorporated into the pit slope design parameters. True = hydrogeology modelled; False = not considered or not applicable.

attributes.name: inter_ramp_angle_deg
attributes.description: The inter-ramp slope angle in degrees, measured between catch berms. Represents the slope angle of the pit wall between successive ramp access levels. Used in geotechnical stability analysis and bench design.

attributes.name: mining_method
attributes.description: The open-cut mining method applied in this pit design. Determines the geometric and operational parameters used in the design (e.g., bench height, slope angles, equipment selection).

attributes.name: optimisation_software
attributes.description: Name of the mine planning software used to generate the pit shell optimisation (e.g., Hexagon MinePlan, Deswik, Whittle). Provides provenance for the design methodology and enables reproducibility of results.

attributes.name: ore_tonnes
attributes.description: Total estimated ore tonnes within the pit design shell above the applied cut-off grade. Derived from the resource block model intersected with the pit shell geometry. Used in LOM scheduling and reserve reporting.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan; Geovia GEMS; JORC Code 2012; CIM Standards; SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: overall_slope_angle_deg
attributes.description: The overall inter-ramp or overall pit slope angle in degrees, representing the angle from horizontal of the pit wall from crest to toe. A critical geotechnical parameter governing pit stability and strip ratio. Typically ranges from 35° to 55° depending on rock mass conditions.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan; Deswik; JORC Code 2012; ISO 14001

attributes.name: pit_bottom_rl_m
attributes.description: The elevation of the pit floor at its lowest point, expressed as a Reduced Level (RL) in metres above mean sea level (AHD or equivalent datum). Defines the maximum depth of the pit design.

attributes.name: pit_crest_rl_m
attributes.description: The elevation of the pit crest (top of the uppermost bench) in metres above mean sea level (AHD or equivalent datum). Together with pit_bottom_rl_m defines the total vertical depth of the pit.

attributes.name: pit_volume_bcm
attributes.description: Total volume of material (ore and waste) within the pit design shell, expressed in Bank Cubic Metres (BCM). Used for LOM scheduling, equipment fleet sizing, and capital cost estimation.

attributes.name: ramp_gradient_pct
attributes.description: The maximum gradient of haul road ramps within the pit expressed as a percentage (rise over run × 100). Governs truck cycle times and fuel consumption. Typically 8–12% for large haul trucks.

attributes.name: ramp_width_m
attributes.description: The design width of haul road ramps within the pit in metres. Determines the minimum turning radius and equipment access for the selected truck fleet. Typically 3–4 times the width of the largest haul truck.

attributes.name: revision_date
attributes.description: Date on which this revision of the pit design was formally issued or updated. Used to track the currency of the design relative to the LOM schedule and resource model.

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: Sequential integer revision number for this pit design, incremented each time the design is formally updated. Enables version control and audit trail of design changes over the LOM planning cycle.

attributes.name: strip_ratio
attributes.description: The ratio of waste tonnes to ore tonnes within the pit design, expressed as tonnes of waste per tonne of ore (t:t). A fundamental economic parameter for open-cut mining — higher strip ratios increase operating costs (OPEX). Calculated as waste_tonnes / ore_tonnes.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan; Deswik; JORC Code 2012; CIM Standards

attributes.name: total_depth_m
attributes.description: The total vertical depth of the pit design in metres, calculated as the difference between pit crest RL and pit bottom RL. A key design parameter for geotechnical stability assessment and LOM planning.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pit design record was last modified in the lakehouse data platform. Used to detect changes and support incremental data processing in the silver layer.

attributes.name: waste_tonnes
attributes.description: Total estimated waste rock tonnes within the pit design shell, including overburden and internal waste. Used to calculate strip ratio and plan waste dump capacity.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan; Geovia GEMS; JORC Code 2012

products.name: stope_design
products.description: Master record of underground stope designs including stope geometry, dimensions, ore drive layouts, pillar specifications, SLC/sublevel configurations, ventilation requirements, and ground support specifications. Captures extraction method (longhole, cut-and-fill, sublevel caving), backfill type and sequence, and design revision history. Sourced from Deswik and Geovia GEMS. Represents the authoritative engineering definition of each underground extraction unit including associated ventilation and ground support requirements.

attributes.name: stope_design_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each stope design record. Primary key for the stope_design data product.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.mine_area. Business justification: A stope design is located within a mine area. This FK enables spatial grouping of underground stope designs by operational mine area. No bidirectional conflict — mine_area does not FK back to stope_de

attributes.name: capex_budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_budget. Business justification: Underground stope development (drives, raises, access) is capital expenditure. Stope designs are approved against CAPEX budgets; finance tracks actual development spend vs approved budget per stope de

attributes.name: commodity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: Stope designs target a specific commodity (copper, nickel, gold). Design parameters — cutoff grade, recovery, dilution — are commodity-specific. Reserve reporting and design approval require commodity

attributes.name: emergency_response_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.emergency_response_plan. Business justification: Underground stope designs must reference the emergency response plan covering the stope area (evacuation routes, refuge chambers, re-entry procedures after blasting). Mining safety regulations require

attributes.name: geological_domain_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.geological_domain. Business justification: Stope designs are constrained by geological domains for ore continuity. Essential for underground mine planning, ensuring extraction respects mineralization boundaries and geotechnical domains.

attributes.name: lom_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.lom_plan. Business justification: Stope designs are part of the overall LOM plan. N:1 relationship (many stope designs in one LOM plan). No bidirectional conflict. Valid planning link.

attributes.name: mine_site_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.mine_site. Business justification: Stope designs are specific to mine sites. Adding mine_site_id FK establishes the site context for underground stope designs. This is a missing normalization for underground operations. No redundant co

attributes.name: mining_block_id
attributes.description: Reference to the mine planning block or stope envelope from which this design was derived. Links to the block model and resource estimation data in Geovia GEMS.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Resource Estimation; Deswik Mine Planning

attributes.name: orebody_id
attributes.description: Reference to the geological orebody or mineralised zone that this stope design targets. Links to the geological resource model for grade, tonnage, and resource classification context.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Geological Modeling; JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101

attributes.name: pit_or_level_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.pit_or_level. Business justification: A stope design is associated with a specific underground level. The pit_or_level entity represents both open-cut pits and underground levels, making this FK essential for locating stope designs within

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.resource_estimate. Business justification: Underground stope designs are optimised against a resource estimate using stope optimiser tools (e.g. Deswik SOT). Reserve reporting and stope design sign-off require a traceable FK to the resource es

attributes.name: risk_assessment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.risk_assessment. Business justification: Underground stope designs require formal geotechnical and ground-fall risk assessments before approval. Mine planning engineers reference the governing risk assessment when approving stope designs — a

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Underground stope designs must remain within tenement boundaries for legal compliance. Critical for resource classification reporting and ensuring extraction rights are valid for designed ore bodies.

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Underground stope designs are developed under capital projects for development capex tracking, engineering cost control, and underground project cost management. Capital project link for underground m

attributes.name: wireframe_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to geology.wireframe. Business justification: Stope designs are bounded by orebody wireframes for extraction planning. Required for underground design, ensuring stopes remain within ore boundaries, and dilution control.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the authorised engineer or geotechnical specialist who formally approved this stope design for construction issue.
attributes.references: MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001; Deswik Stope Optimization

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which the stope design was formally approved by the authorised geotechnical or mine planning engineer, permitting issue for construction. Null if not yet approved.
attributes.references: MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

attributes.name: backfill_strength_mpa
attributes.description: Specified minimum unconfined compressive strength (UCS) of the cemented backfill in megapascals (MPa) at the design cure time. Applicable only to cemented paste fill and cemented rock fill designs. Drives cement binder content and backfill plant mix design.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001

attributes.name: backfill_type
attributes.description: Type of backfill material specified for this stope design after ore extraction. Determines geotechnical stability of adjacent stopes, backfill plant requirements, and extraction sequence constraints. None indicates open stoping without backfill.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this stope design record was first created in the data platform, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: cutoff_grade
attributes.description: Minimum economic grade threshold applied to define the stope boundary and determine ore versus waste classification within the design. Expressed in the same unit as design_grade_primary. Directly impacts designed ore tonnes and LOM economics.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards; SAMREC Code

attributes.name: design_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current revision of the stope design was formally completed and issued by the mine design engineer.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: design_grade_primary
attributes.description: Estimated in-situ grade of the primary commodity within the designed stope boundary, expressed in the commodity-appropriate unit (g/t for gold/silver, % for base metals). Derived from the block model and used for mill feed planning and revenue forecasting.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Resource Estimation; JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC Code

attributes.name: design_revision
attributes.description: Sequential revision number of the stope design, incremented each time the design is formally updated. Revision 0 represents the initial issue; subsequent revisions capture engineering changes, geotechnical updates, or grade re-interpretations.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; ISO 19650 Information Management

attributes.name: design_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the stope design record, tracking progression from initial draft through engineering review, approval, and construction issue. Superseded status indicates a newer revision has replaced this design.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; ISO 19650 Information Management

attributes.name: designed_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the mine design engineer responsible for authoring this stope design revision.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; SAP S/4HANA HR

attributes.name: designed_dilution_pct
attributes.description: Planned dilution percentage representing the proportion of waste rock expected to be extracted with the ore due to stope geometry and mining method. Expressed as a percentage of total ROM tonnes. Key input to mill feed grade forecasting.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards

attributes.name: designed_ore_tonnes
attributes.description: Estimated in-situ ore tonnage within the designed stope boundary, calculated from the block model grade-tonnage curve. Represents the planned ore extraction quantity before dilution and recovery adjustments.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Resource Estimation; JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards

attributes.name: designed_recovery_pct
attributes.description: Planned ore recovery percentage representing the proportion of in-situ ore tonnes expected to be extracted from the stope. Accounts for ore loss to pillars, hangingwall slough, and extraction method limitations.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards

attributes.name: designed_volume_m3
attributes.description: Total designed void volume of the stope in cubic metres as calculated from the 3D stope solid in Deswik or Geovia GEMS. Used for backfill volume estimation, blast design, and ventilation requirements.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: deswik_stope_reference
attributes.description: Native stope identifier from the Deswik mine planning and stope optimisation system. Enables reconciliation between the silver layer data product and the Deswik source system for scheduling and optimisation workflows.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Deswik Mine Planning and Scheduling

attributes.name: extraction_method
attributes.description: Underground mining extraction method applied to this stope design. Determines drill pattern, blast design, support requirements, and backfill strategy. Key driver of dilution, recovery rate, and OPEX. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: longhole_open|longhole_retreat|cut_and_fill|sublevel_caving|sublevel_stoping|bench_and_fill|room_and_pillar|shrinkage — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards

attributes.name: extraction_sequence
attributes.description: Planned extraction sequence number of this stope within its mining block or production area. Governs the order of stope firing to manage geotechnical stability, backfill curing time, and ventilation circuit integrity.
attributes.references: Deswik Mine Planning and Scheduling; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: geovia_gems_stope_reference
attributes.description: Native stope object identifier from the Geovia GEMS geological modelling and mine design system. Used for traceability and data lineage between the silver layer data product and the source system of record.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Mine Design; SAP S/4HANA PS

attributes.name: grade_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the primary commodity grade value (e.g., g/t for gold, % for copper or iron ore, ppm for trace elements). Ensures correct interpretation of design_grade_primary across different commodity types.

attributes.name: ground_support_class
attributes.description: Geotechnical ground support classification assigned to the stope design, typically based on rock mass rating (RMR) or Q-system. Drives the specification of rock bolts, cable bolts, mesh, and shotcrete requirements. Class A = competent rock; Class E = very poor ground.
attributes.references: MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001; Deswik Stope Optimization

attributes.name: level_elevation_m
attributes.description: Elevation in metres above mean sea level (mAMSL) of the primary extraction level or ore drive floor for this stope design. Used for ventilation circuit design, dewatering planning, and LOM scheduling.
attributes.references: Geovia GEMS Mine Design; Deswik Mine Planning; GIS Coordinate Reference Systems

attributes.name: lom_schedule_period
attributes.description: Life of Mine (LOM) planning period or fiscal year-quarter in which this stope is scheduled for extraction (e.g., 'FY2026-Q2'). Links the stope design to the LOM production schedule in Deswik for NPV and IRR modelling.
attributes.references: Deswik Mine Planning and Scheduling; SAP S/4HANA CO; IFRS 6 Exploration

attributes.name: ore_drive_count
attributes.description: Number of ore drives (extraction drives) designed within the stope footprint. Determines development metres required, drill rig access, and mucking logistics for the stope.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: ore_drive_height_m
attributes.description: Designed height of each ore drive (extraction drive) within the stope in metres. Determines equipment clearance and development cost per metre.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: ore_drive_width_m
attributes.description: Designed width of each ore drive (extraction drive) within the stope in metres. Determines equipment clearance, drill pattern geometry, and development cost per metre.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: pillar_type
attributes.description: Type of geotechnical pillar incorporated into the stope design to maintain ground stability. Crown pillars separate stopes vertically; rib pillars separate stopes horizontally; sill pillars provide floor support; barrier pillars protect major infrastructure. None indicates pillarless design.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001

attributes.name: pillar_width_m
attributes.description: Designed width of the geotechnical pillar in metres. Null if no pillar is specified (pillar_type = none). Critical geotechnical parameter determining pillar stability factor and ore loss to pillars.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57; ISO 45001

attributes.name: stope_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the stope design within the mine planning system. Used as the primary business reference across Deswik, Geovia GEMS, and SAP PS work breakdown structures.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design; SAP PS Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

attributes.name: stope_height_m
attributes.description: Designed vertical height of the stope from floor to back (crown) in metres. Critical input for geotechnical stability assessment, cable bolt design, and blast energy calculations.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design; MSHA 30 CFR Part 57

attributes.name: stope_length_m
attributes.description: Designed horizontal length of the stope along the strike direction in metres. Primary dimension used for volume calculation, drill pattern design, and production scheduling.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: stope_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label assigned to the stope design, typically incorporating level, drive, and sequence identifiers (e.g., 'L15-OD-001'). Used in engineering drawings, P&IDs, and operational communications.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: stope_width_m
attributes.description: Designed horizontal width of the stope across the orebody in metres. Determines minimum mining width, dilution exposure, and equipment access requirements.
attributes.references: Deswik Stope Optimization; Geovia GEMS Mine Design

attributes.name: sublevel_interval_m
attributes.description: Vertical distance in metres between sublevels within the stope design, applicable to sublevel caving (SLC) and sublevel stoping extraction methods. Drives drill ring burden, blast design, and ore recovery modelling.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this stope design record was most recently modified in the data platform, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Tracks design revision history and supports change management auditing.

attributes.name: ventilation_requirement_m3s
attributes.business_glossary_term: Ventilation Airflow Requirement (cubic metres per second)
attributes.description: Minimum required fresh air supply to the stope in cubic metres per second (m³/s) during active extraction, as specified in the stope design. Determined by diesel equipment fleet, blast fume clearance time, and regulatory minimum airflow standards.
attributes.references: MSHA 30 CFR Part 57 Ventilation; ISO 45001; Deswik Mine Planning

products.name: lom_plan
products.description: Life of Mine (LOM) plan master record capturing the long-term production schedule, annual ore and waste movement targets, strip ratio projections, cut-off grade assumptions, NPV/IRR parameters, and CAPEX/OPEX phasing across the full mine life. Sourced from Deswik and Hexagon MinePlan. The SSOT for strategic mine planning.

attributes.name: lom_plan_id

attributes.name: saleable_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.saleable_product. Business justification: LOM financial modelling (NPV, IRR, pricing assumptions) is performed against specific saleable product specifications and pricing. A domain expert expects the LOM plan to reference the saleable produc

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: LOM plans must reference the primary tenement for JORC/NI 43-101 reserve reporting, regulatory submissions, and legal mining authority verification. Essential for competent person sign-off and ASX/SEC

attributes.name: aisc_usd_per_t
attributes.description: All-In Sustaining Cost (AISC) per tonne, expressed in USD. Includes C1 cash costs plus sustaining CAPEX, royalties, and corporate G&A. Provides a comprehensive cost measure for economic viability assessment and investor disclosure.
attributes.references: World Gold Council AISC Standard 2018; ICMM; SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this LOM plan version received formal executive or board approval. Marks the transition from 'under_review' to 'approved' status and triggers downstream planning and budgeting activities.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; SEC S-K 1300; SAP S/4HANA PS project governance

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the executive or technical authority who formally approved this LOM plan version. Required for governance, audit trail, and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; ISO 14001; ICMM governance framework; SAP S/4HANA PS

attributes.name: average_annual_ore_mt
attributes.description: The average annual ore extraction rate in million tonnes per year (Mtpa) over the full LOM plan. Used for steady-state OPEX modelling, workforce planning, and long-term supply agreements.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Deswik production scheduling; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: average_ore_grade
attributes.description: The average head grade of the ore reserve included in the LOM plan, expressed in the same unit as cutoff_grade_unit. A key input to revenue and concentrate production forecasts.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; Geovia GEMS resource estimation

attributes.name: c1_cash_cost_usd_per_t
attributes.description: The C1 Cash Cost per tonne of ore or concentrate produced, expressed in USD. Represents direct cash costs of mining and processing excluding royalties, depreciation, and sustaining capital. Industry-standard cost metric for benchmarking and investor reporting.
attributes.references: World Gold Council Cost Reporting Standard; ICMM; Brook Hunt C1 methodology

attributes.name: commodity_price_assumption_usd
attributes.description: The long-term commodity price assumption used in the LOM financial model, expressed in USD per tonne (or per lb/oz as applicable). A critical sensitivity input; changes to this assumption materially affect NPV and IRR outcomes.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this LOM plan record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; Databricks Lakehouse audit standards; ICMM data governance

attributes.name: cutoff_grade
attributes.description: The minimum economic grade of ore included in the LOM plan reserve, below which material is classified as waste. Expressed in the commodity-appropriate unit (e.g., % Fe for iron ore, % Cu for copper, g/t Au for gold). Drives ore/waste classification and reserve estimation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: cutoff_grade_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the cut-off grade value (e.g., 'pct' for percentage Fe/Cu, 'g_per_t' for grams per tonne Au/Ag, 'ppm' for parts per million). Required to correctly interpret the cutoff_grade field.

attributes.name: discount_rate_pct
attributes.description: The real or nominal discount rate (%) applied in the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model to calculate the NPV of the LOM plan. Typically represents the Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) or a project-specific hurdle rate.
attributes.references: IFRS 6; SEC S-K 1300; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: exchange_rate_assumption
attributes.description: The foreign exchange rate assumption used in the LOM financial model (e.g., AUD/USD, CLP/USD). Applied to convert local currency OPEX and CAPEX to USD for NPV/IRR calculations. A key sensitivity variable in the financial model.
attributes.references: IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI; SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: irr_pct
attributes.description: Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of the LOM plan expressed as a percentage. The discount rate at which the NPV of the project equals zero. Used alongside NPV as a primary investment hurdle metric for project sanctioning.
attributes.references: IFRS 6; SEC S-K 1300; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: lom_strip_ratio
attributes.description: The overall Life of Mine strip ratio, expressed as tonnes of waste per tonne of ore (t:t). A key economic indicator representing the ratio of overburden to ore that must be moved to extract the ore reserve. Calculated as total_waste_mt / total_ore_reserve_mt.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards 2014; Deswik scheduling

attributes.name: mine_life_years
attributes.description: Total planned duration of the mine life in years, from first ore extraction to final closure. Derived from plan_start_date and plan_end_date for planning purposes; stored explicitly for reporting and regulatory disclosure.

attributes.name: mining_method
attributes.description: Primary mining method employed in this LOM plan. 'open_cut' refers to open-pit operations; 'underground' includes methods such as Sub-Level Caving (SLC) and longwall; 'open_cut_underground' indicates a combined operation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards 2014; Deswik method classification

attributes.name: npv_musd
attributes.description: Net Present Value (NPV) of the LOM plan in millions of USD, calculated using the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) methodology at the specified discount rate. Primary financial metric for investment decision-making and project approval.
attributes.references: IFRS 6; SEC S-K 1300; NI 43-101; CIM Definition Standards 2014; ICMM

attributes.name: peak_annual_ore_mt
attributes.description: The maximum planned annual ore extraction rate in million tonnes per year (Mtpa) over the LOM plan. Used for infrastructure sizing, processing plant capacity planning, and peak CAPEX determination.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Deswik production scheduling; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: plan_code
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the LOM plan, typically assigned by the mine planning team in Deswik or Hexagon MinePlan. Format: LOM-{SITE}-{YEAR}. Used for cross-system referencing and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: plan_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Life of Mine (LOM) Plan End Date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the LOM plan production schedule concludes, representing the projected end of mine life including rehabilitation and closure activities.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; ISO 14001; Mine Rehabilitation and Closure standards

attributes.name: plan_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the LOM plan (e.g., 'Pilbara Iron Ore LOM 2024 Base Case'). Used for identification in planning reports and executive dashboards.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Hexagon MinePlan naming conventions

attributes.name: plan_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Life of Mine (LOM) Plan Start Date
attributes.description: The calendar date from which the LOM plan production schedule commences. Represents the effective start of the planned mine life, aligned with the first scheduled ore extraction period.

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the LOM plan. 'draft' indicates work-in-progress; 'under_review' indicates pending technical and executive sign-off; 'approved' is the active SSOT plan; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer version; 'archived' indicates retired from active use.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; CIM Definition Standards 2014; ISO 14001

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: Classification of the LOM plan scenario. 'base_case' is the primary planning scenario; 'upside_case' and 'downside_case' represent sensitivity scenarios; 'closure_case' models mine rehabilitation; 'feasibility' is used for pre-production studies.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: plan_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the LOM plan (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.3'). Enables tracking of iterative revisions and scenario comparisons over the mine life planning cycle.
attributes.references: Deswik LOM versioning conventions; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: planned_recovery_rate_pct
attributes.description: The planned metallurgical recovery rate expressed as a percentage, representing the proportion of the valuable mineral extracted from the ore during processing. A critical input to concentrate production and revenue forecasting in the LOM plan.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; Mineral Processing and Beneficiation standards

attributes.name: probable_reserve_mt
attributes.description: Probable Ore Reserve category in million tonnes, as defined by JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC. Lower geological confidence than Proved Reserve but still economically viable and included in the LOM production schedule.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300; IFRS 6

attributes.name: proved_reserve_mt
attributes.description: Highest-confidence ore reserve category (Proved Reserve) in million tonnes, as defined by JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC. Represents the portion of the ore body with the greatest geological certainty, used in bankable feasibility studies and investor disclosures.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300; IFRS 6

attributes.name: reporting_standard
attributes.description: The mineral resource and reserve reporting standard under which this LOM plan has been prepared and disclosed (e.g., JORC for Australia, NI 43-101 for Canada, SAMREC for South Africa, SEC S-K 1300 for US-listed companies).
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: resource_classification
attributes.description: The highest mineral resource classification category underpinning the LOM plan per JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC standards. 'measured' is highest confidence, 'indicated' is moderate, 'inferred' is lowest. Determines the regulatory disclosure obligations for the plan.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300; CIM Definition Standards 2014

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this LOM plan was sourced or generated (e.g., Deswik, Hexagon MinePlan, Geovia GEMS). Supports data lineage tracking and Silver Layer provenance in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse data lineage standards; Deswik; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: total_capex_musd
attributes.description: Total planned Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) over the full mine life in millions of USD, including pre-production development, sustaining capital, and closure/rehabilitation costs. A primary input to NPV and IRR calculations in the LOM financial model.
attributes.references: IFRS 6; SAP S/4HANA CO-PA; ICMM reporting guidelines; SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: total_opex_musd
attributes.description: Total planned Operating Expenditure (OPEX) over the full mine life in millions of USD, encompassing mining, processing, G&A, and site services costs. Used in conjunction with revenue forecasts to derive LOM cash flow projections.
attributes.references: IFRS 6; SAP S/4HANA CO-PA; ICMM reporting guidelines; SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: total_ore_reserve_mt
attributes.description: Total Proved and Probable Ore Reserve underpinning the LOM plan, expressed in million tonnes (Mt). Classified per JORC/NI 43-101/SAMREC standards. This is the primary ore inventory figure driving the production schedule.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; NI 43-101; SAMREC 2016; SEC S-K 1300

attributes.name: total_waste_mt
attributes.description: Total planned waste rock and overburden movement over the full mine life in million tonnes. Used to calculate the Life of Mine (LOM) strip ratio and plan waste dump infrastructure and haulage requirements.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012; Deswik mine scheduling; Hexagon MinePlan

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this LOM plan record was last modified in the data platform. Used to detect changes, support incremental processing, and maintain audit trail integrity in the Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; Databricks Lakehouse audit standards; ICMM data governance

products.name: production_schedule

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.pit_design. Business justification: Production schedules are executed against a pit design. N:1 relationship (many schedules for one pit design). No bidirectional conflict. Valid planning link. Complements existing pit_or_stope_id gener

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.pit_or_level. Business justification: A production schedule is planned for a specific pit or level. This FK links the schedule to the operational pit/level entity, enabling schedule filtering and reporting by pit or underground level. No

attributes.name: resource_estimate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.resource_estimate. Business justification: Production schedules reference resource estimates for tonnage and grade planning. Schedulers validate planned extraction against the resource estimate to ensure compliance with reserve declarations an
