attributes.name: laboratory_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.laboratory. Business justification: Sample preparation is performed at a specific laboratory (may be different from the analytical laboratory). Currently sample_preparation has preparation_laboratory_code and preparation_laboratory_name

attributes.name: laboratory_sample_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.laboratory_sample. Business justification: Sample preparation tracks the physical preparation steps applied to each sample prior to analysis. The primary parent of a preparation record is the laboratory_sample being prepared. Currently sample_

attributes.name: maintenance_work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.work_order. Business justification: Sample preparation records for maintenance-related samples need work order traceability for audit trails, quality control verification, and chain of custody documentation in mining operations where sa

attributes.name: risk_assessment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.risk_assessment. Business justification: Sample preparation (crushing, pulverizing, acid digestion) involves physical and chemical hazards requiring a documented risk assessment (JSEA/JHA) before commencement. Mining HSE systems mandate this

attributes.name: sample_batch_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the preparation batch if multiple samples were prepared together. Supports batch-level quality control and traceability.

attributes.name: actual_turnaround_time_hours
attributes.description: Actual time taken to complete the preparation, measured in hours. Used for performance monitoring and SLA compliance.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the preparation was approved by the supervisor or quality manager. Marks formal acceptance of preparation quality.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Identifier of the supervisor or quality manager who approved the preparation results. Required for quality assurance sign-off.

attributes.name: chain_of_custody_verified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether chain-of-custody was verified and maintained during preparation. True if verified, false otherwise.

attributes.name: contamination_risk_level
attributes.description: Assessment of contamination risk during preparation based on equipment history, sample type, and preparation method. Used for contamination investigation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the sample preparation record was first created in the LIMS system. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: drying_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Duration for which the sample was dried, measured in minutes. Ensures consistent moisture removal across samples.

attributes.name: drying_temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Temperature at which the sample was dried during preparation, measured in degrees Celsius. Critical for moisture removal and sample stability.

attributes.name: equipment_type
attributes.description: Type of equipment used for the preparation step (e.g., crusher, pulverizer, splitter, dryer, sieve). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: crusher|pulverizer|splitter|dryer|sieve|grinder|mill|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this preparation record is currently active. False if the record has been superseded or voided.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the sample preparation record was last updated in the LIMS system. Audit trail field.

attributes.name: moisture_content_percent
attributes.description: Moisture content of the sample measured during or after preparation, expressed as a percentage. Critical for dry weight calculations and assay corrections.

attributes.name: operator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the laboratory technician or operator who performed the sample preparation.

attributes.name: original_sample_weight_kg
attributes.description: Weight of the original sample received for preparation, measured in kilograms. Baseline for mass balance calculations.

attributes.name: particle_size_actual_microns
attributes.description: Actual particle size achieved after preparation, measured in microns. Used to verify preparation quality and compliance with analytical requirements.

attributes.name: particle_size_target_microns
attributes.description: Target particle size for the prepared sample, measured in microns. Defines the fineness required for subsequent analytical methods.

attributes.name: preparation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the sample preparation was performed. Critical for chain-of-custody tracking and sample integrity assessment.

attributes.name: preparation_method_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the preparation method applied (e.g., CRUSH, PULV, SPLIT, DRY, SIEVE). Defines the specific preparation protocol used.

attributes.name: preparation_method_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the preparation method applied, including specific steps, equipment settings, and protocols followed.

attributes.name: preparation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing any deviations, observations, or issues encountered during sample preparation. Supports investigation and audit trails.

attributes.name: preparation_priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the sample preparation, determining processing sequence and turnaround time.

attributes.name: preparation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the sample preparation workflow. Tracks progress from initiation to completion.

attributes.name: preparation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the sample preparation was completed. Supports detailed chain-of-custody and workflow tracking.

attributes.name: pulp_weight_kg
attributes.description: Weight of the fine pulp or prepared sample after preparation, measured in kilograms. This is the material sent for analysis.

attributes.name: qaqc_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this preparation is part of a QA/QC program (e.g., duplicate, blank, standard). True if QA/QC sample, false otherwise.

attributes.name: qaqc_sample_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Sample Type
attributes.description: Type of QA/QC sample if applicable (e.g., duplicate, blank, certified reference material, field duplicate). None if not a QA/QC sample.

attributes.name: reject_weight_kg
attributes.description: Weight of the coarse reject material removed during preparation (e.g., after crushing or sieving), measured in kilograms. Used for mass balance verification.

attributes.name: sieve_size_mesh
attributes.description: Mesh size of the sieve used during preparation (e.g., 100, 200, 400 mesh). Defines the particle size separation applied.

attributes.name: splitting_method
attributes.description: Method used to split or sub-sample the prepared material (e.g., riffle splitter, rotary splitter, cone and quarter). Ensures representative sub-sampling.

attributes.name: turnaround_time_hours
attributes.description: Target turnaround time for completing the preparation, measured in hours from receipt to completion.

products.name: qaqc_sample
products.description: Master record for QA/QC control samples inserted into sample streams, including certified reference materials (CRMs), blanks, field duplicates, and pulp duplicates. Stores QA/QC sample type, insertion position, expected grade, tolerance range, and associated batch. Enables systematic monitoring of laboratory accuracy, precision, and contamination per JORC and NI 43-101 QA/QC requirements.
products.reference: JORC QA/QC Protocol / LabWare LIMS QC Sample

attributes.name: qaqc_sample_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Sample Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the QA/QC control sample record. Primary key.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3 - Sampling Techniques and Data; NI 43-101 Section 11 - Sample Preparation, Analyses and Security

attributes.name: analytical_method_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.analytical_method. Business justification: QA/QC samples are analyzed using a specific analytical method. Currently qaqc_sample has analytical_method (STRING) but no FK. Adding analytical_method_id FK links to the method specification used for

attributes.name: crm_standard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.crm_standard. Business justification: QA/QC control samples reference certified reference materials (CRMs). Currently qaqc_sample has crm_certificate_number and crm_supplier (STRING) but no FK. Adding crm_standard_id FK links to the full

attributes.name: grade_parameter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.grade_parameter. Business justification: analyte_code on qaqc_sample is a denormalization of grade_parameter (lims_parameter_code). QAQC samples validate specific grade parameters; this FK enables parameter-level QAQC performance tracking, b

attributes.name: laboratory_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.laboratory. Business justification: QA/QC samples are analyzed at a specific laboratory. Currently qaqc_sample has laboratory_code (STRING) but no FK. Adding laboratory_id FK links to the laboratory that analyzed the control sample, ena

attributes.name: laboratory_sample_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original production sample from which a duplicate QA/QC sample was created (field duplicate, pulp duplicate, coarse duplicate). Null for CRMs, blanks, and standards. Enables paired comparison for precision analysis.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Sample Lineage; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

attributes.name: sample_batch_id
attributes.description: Reference to the analytical batch into which this QA/QC sample was inserted. Links to the parent batch for traceability and batch-level QA/QC reporting.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Batch Management; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

attributes.name: specification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.specification. Business justification: QAQC samples are inserted into batches to verify that analytical results meet tolerance limits defined in a product specification. The tolerance_lower, tolerance_upper, and expected_grade fields on qa

attributes.name: absolute_difference
attributes.description: Absolute difference between assay_result and expected_grade (assay_result - expected_grade), expressed in the same unit. Used for precision analysis of duplicate samples and accuracy assessment of CRMs.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Statistical Quality Control Methods

attributes.name: analysis_date
attributes.description: Date the QA/QC sample was analyzed by the laboratory. Used to track analytical delays and correlate QA/QC performance with laboratory workload and instrument calibration cycles.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date the QA/QC result was formally approved by a qualified person. Null if pending approval. Used for audit trails and regulatory reporting timelines.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; NI 43-101 Competent Person Requirements

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the qualified person (geologist, metallurgist, QA/QC manager) who reviewed and approved this QA/QC result. Null if pending approval. Required for JORC/NI 43-101 competent person sign-off.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; NI 43-101 Competent Person Requirements

attributes.name: assay_result
attributes.description: Actual analytical result returned by the laboratory for this QA/QC sample, expressed in the same unit as expected_grade. Compared against expected_grade and tolerance limits to determine pass/fail status and calculate bias/precision metrics.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Assay Results; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

attributes.name: assay_result_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the assay result. Must match expected_grade_unit for valid comparison. Percent (%) for major elements, parts per million (ppm) for trace elements, grams per tonne (g/t) for precious metals.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Unit Standards; SI Units and Mining Industry Standards

attributes.name: batch_reanalysis_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the entire sample batch must be reanalyzed due to systematic QA/QC failure (e.g., multiple CRM failures, blank contamination, duplicate precision failure). True triggers batch rejection and resubmission workflow.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

attributes.name: bias_percent
attributes.description: Calculated percentage difference between assay_result and expected_grade, expressed as ((assay_result - expected_grade) / expected_grade) * 100. Positive values indicate over-reporting, negative values indicate under-reporting. Used to assess laboratory accuracy and systematic error.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Statistical Quality Control Methods

attributes.name: certified_standard_deviation
attributes.description: Certified standard deviation for CRM samples as documented in the supplier certificate. Null for non-CRM QA/QC sample types. Used to calculate statistical control limits and assess laboratory precision against certified variability.
attributes.references: CRM Certificate Documentation; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or context regarding this QA/QC sample (e.g., sample handling issues, laboratory comments, unusual results). Supports audit trails and knowledge capture.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Sample Comments; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QA/QC sample record was first created in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: detection_limit
attributes.description: Lower detection limit of the analytical method for the target analyte, expressed in the same unit as assay_result. Results below this value are typically reported as less-than (<) values. Critical for blank sample evaluation.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Method Detection Limits; ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: expected_grade
attributes.description: Certified or expected assay grade for the QA/QC sample, expressed in the same unit as the target analyte (e.g., % for iron ore, ppm for gold, g/t for precious metals). For CRMs, this is the certified value; for blanks, this is typically zero or below detection limit; for duplicates, this is the original sample grade.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; NI 43-101 Section 11; CRM Certificate Documentation

attributes.name: expected_grade_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the expected grade value. Percent (%) for major elements, parts per million (ppm) for trace elements, grams per tonne (g/t) for precious metals, ounces per ton (oz/t) for imperial systems, milligrams per kilogram (mg/kg) for environmental samples.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; SI Units and Mining Industry Standards

attributes.name: insertion_ratio
attributes.description: Target insertion frequency of this QA/QC sample type expressed as a percentage of total samples (e.g., 5.00 means 1 in 20 samples). Used to validate compliance with QA/QC protocols and JORC/NI 43-101 requirements.

attributes.name: insertion_sequence
attributes.description: Sequential position of the QA/QC sample within the batch submission stream. Used to verify insertion frequency and systematic placement per QA/QC protocols (e.g., 1 CRM per 20 samples, 1 blank per 40 samples).
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

attributes.name: investigation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field documenting investigation findings, root cause analysis, and corrective actions taken for failed QA/QC samples. Null if no investigation required. Critical for audit trails and continuous improvement.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; ISO/IEC 17025 Corrective Action Requirements

attributes.name: investigation_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this QA/QC result requires formal investigation due to failure, systematic bias, or contamination. True triggers investigation workflow per JORC/NI 43-101 requirements.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

attributes.name: laboratory_job_number
attributes.description: External job or work order number assigned by the laboratory for this batch submission. Used for cross-referencing with laboratory certificates and invoices.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS External Reference; Laboratory Certificate Documentation

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QA/QC sample record was last modified in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Used for audit trails and change tracking.

attributes.name: preparation_method
attributes.description: Sample preparation technique applied before analysis (e.g., crush_to_minus_2mm, pulverize_to_85pct_minus_75um, dry_at_105c, digest_four_acid). Critical for duplicate QA/QC samples to ensure preparation consistency.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Preparation Protocols; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

attributes.name: qaqc_sample_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Sample Number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier for the QA/QC sample, typically following laboratory naming conventions (e.g., CRM-2023-001, BLK-001, DUP-045). Used for sample tracking and audit trails.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Sample Numbering; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

attributes.name: qaqc_sample_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Sample Type
attributes.description: Classification of the QA/QC control sample type. Certified Reference Material (CRM) validates accuracy, blanks detect contamination, field duplicates assess sampling precision, pulp duplicates assess analytical precision, coarse duplicates assess crushing/splitting precision, and standards validate instrument calibration.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3 - QA/QC Procedures; NI 43-101 Section 11; SAMREC Code 2016

attributes.name: qaqc_status
attributes.description: Pass/fail status of the QA/QC sample based on comparison of assay_result against tolerance limits. Pass indicates result within acceptable range, fail triggers investigation and potential batch rejection, warning indicates borderline result, pending awaits analysis, not_analyzed indicates sample not yet processed.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date the QA/QC sample was submitted to the laboratory as part of the batch. Used for turnaround time tracking and temporal QA/QC trend analysis.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Submission Tracking; JORC Code 2012 Section 3

attributes.name: tolerance_lower
attributes.description: Lower acceptable limit for assay results, typically defined as expected_grade minus acceptable variance (e.g., 2 standard deviations for CRMs, detection limit for blanks). Results below this threshold trigger QA/QC failure flags and investigation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

attributes.name: tolerance_type
attributes.description: Method used to define tolerance limits. Absolute uses fixed grade units, relative_percent uses percentage of expected grade, standard_deviation uses statistical variance from certified mean. Determines how tolerance_lower and tolerance_upper are calculated.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Statistical Quality Control Methods

attributes.name: tolerance_upper
attributes.description: Upper acceptable limit for assay results, typically defined as expected_grade plus acceptable variance (e.g., 2 standard deviations for CRMs, maximum contamination threshold for blanks). Results above this threshold trigger QA/QC failure flags and investigation.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Section 3; Laboratory QA/QC Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

products.name: qaqc_result
products.description: Records the analytical result for each QA/QC control sample and its pass/fail assessment against acceptance criteria. Captures reported value, expected value, z-score, percent relative difference (PRD), bias flag, failure reason, and corrective action triggered. Provides the audit trail required for JORC Table 1 QA/QC disclosure and resource estimation sign-off.
products.reference: JORC Table 1 QA/QC / LabWare LIMS QC Result

attributes.name: qaqc_result_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Result Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the QA/QC result record. Primary key for the qaqc_result data product.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - QA/QC Procedures

attributes.name: analytical_method_id
attributes.description: FK to laboratory.analytical_method

attributes.name: corrective_action_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.corrective_action. Business justification: qaqc_result has corrective_action_required and corrective_action_description fields but no FK to the corrective_action record. ISO 17025 requires QAQC result failures to generate traceable corrective

attributes.name: grade_parameter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.grade_parameter. Business justification: The analyte field on qaqc_result is a denormalization of grade_parameter. QAQC results control specific grade parameters; this FK enables parameter-level control chart analysis, bias detection, and co

attributes.name: instrument_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.instrument. Business justification: QA/QC results are generated by specific analytical instruments. Linking qaqc_result to instrument enables instrument-level QA/QC performance monitoring, identification of systematic bias or drift in s

attributes.name: laboratory_id
attributes.description: Reference to the laboratory that performed the analysis. Used to track performance by laboratory and support multi-laboratory quality comparisons.

attributes.name: qaqc_sample_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Sample Identifier
attributes.description: Reference to the control sample that was analyzed. Links to the sample record in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS).

attributes.name: sample_batch_id
attributes.description: Reference to the analytical batch in which this QA/QC sample was processed. Used to group samples analyzed together for quality control assessment.

attributes.name: specification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.specification. Business justification: QAQC results are evaluated against specification control limits to determine batch compliance for product release. The jorc_table_1_reference and resource_estimation_approved fields confirm regulatory

attributes.name: absolute_difference
attributes.description: The absolute difference between the reported value and expected value. Calculated as |reported_value - expected_value|. Used for low-grade samples where relative measures may be misleading.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - QA/QC Metrics

attributes.name: analysis_date
attributes.description: The date on which the QA/QC sample was analyzed by the laboratory. Used for temporal quality trend analysis and batch traceability.

attributes.name: analysis_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the analytical measurement was completed. Provides high-resolution temporal tracking for quality control and audit purposes.

attributes.name: bias_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether systematic bias has been detected in the analytical results. True indicates bias is present (consistently high or low results), false indicates no bias detected.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - Accuracy and Bias

attributes.name: contamination_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether contamination has been detected based on blank sample results. True indicates contamination is present, false indicates no contamination detected.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - Contamination Control

attributes.name: control_sample_number
attributes.description: The unique identifier or barcode assigned to the physical QA/QC control sample submitted for analysis.

attributes.name: control_sample_type
attributes.description: Type of QA/QC control sample analyzed. Blank samples detect contamination, standards verify calibration, duplicates assess precision, and certified reference materials (CRM) verify accuracy.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - Sample Analysis and QA/QC

attributes.name: corrective_action_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether corrective action is required in response to this QA/QC failure. True triggers workflow for investigation and remediation, false indicates no action needed.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this QA/QC result record was first created in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Provides audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: expected_value
attributes.description: The expected or certified value for the control sample. For standards and certified reference materials (CRM), this is the known concentration. For blanks, this is typically zero. For duplicates, this is the original sample value.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - QA/QC Standards

attributes.name: failure_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the QA/QC result failed acceptance criteria. Includes specific metrics that were out of range and potential root causes identified during investigation.

attributes.name: jorc_table_1_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Joint Ore Reserves Committee (JORC) Table 1 Reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific section of the JORC Code Table 1 documentation where this QA/QC result is disclosed. Required for public reporting of mineral resources and ore reserves.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this QA/QC result record was last updated. Tracks changes to pass/fail status, corrective actions, or review outcomes.

attributes.name: lower_control_limit
attributes.description: The lower acceptable threshold for the QA/QC result. Values below this limit indicate a potential quality issue requiring investigation.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - QA/QC Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: pass_fail_status
attributes.description: The overall assessment of whether the QA/QC result meets acceptance criteria. Pass indicates the result is within control limits, fail indicates a quality issue, warning indicates borderline performance, and under investigation indicates pending review.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - QA/QC Assessment

attributes.name: percent_relative_difference
attributes.description: The relative difference between reported and expected values expressed as a percentage. Calculated as ((reported_value - expected_value) / expected_value) * 100. Key metric for duplicate precision assessment.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - Precision and Accuracy

attributes.name: precision_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether precision issues have been detected based on duplicate sample results. True indicates poor precision (high variability), false indicates acceptable precision.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - Precision Assessment

attributes.name: reported_value
attributes.description: The analytical result value reported by the laboratory for this QA/QC control sample. Measured in the unit of measure specified for the analyte.

attributes.name: resource_estimation_approved
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the associated analytical batch has been approved for use in resource estimation based on QA/QC performance. True indicates data is suitable for JORC resource calculations, false indicates data quality issues prevent use.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - Data Suitability for Resource Estimation

attributes.name: review_comments
attributes.description: Additional comments or observations recorded by the reviewer during the QA/QC assessment. May include context for borderline results or justification for acceptance decisions.

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: The date on which the QA/QC result was reviewed and the pass/fail assessment was finalized. Critical for audit trail and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - QA/QC Review Process

attributes.name: reviewed_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the qualified person (QP) or laboratory supervisor who reviewed and approved the QA/QC result assessment. Required for JORC Table 1 compliance.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - Competent Person Sign-off

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit in which the reported and expected values are expressed. Common units include parts per million (ppm), parts per billion (ppb), percent (%), grams per tonne (g/t), and ounces per ton (oz/t).

attributes.name: upper_control_limit
attributes.description: The upper acceptable threshold for the QA/QC result. Values above this limit indicate a potential quality issue requiring investigation.
attributes.references: JORC Code Table 1 Section 3 - QA/QC Acceptance Criteria

attributes.name: z_score
attributes.description: The number of standard deviations the reported value is from the expected value. Calculated as (reported_value - expected_value) / standard_deviation. Used to assess the statistical significance of deviations.
attributes.references: ISO 13528 Statistical Methods for Proficiency Testing

products.name: analytical_method
products.description: Reference catalogue of all approved analytical methods used in the laboratory, including fire assay (FA-AAS, FA-OES), XRF (pressed pellet, fused bead), ICP-MS, ICP-OES, LECO carbon/sulphur, and titration. Stores method code, analyte list, detection limits, upper limits, matrix applicability, accreditation standard (NATA, ISO 17025), and method version. Governs which methods are approved for resource estimation versus process control.

attributes.name: analytical_method_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the analytical method record. Primary key.

attributes.name: accreditation_number
attributes.description: Unique accreditation certificate or registration number issued by the accrediting body for this specific method. Used for audit trails and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: accreditation_standard
attributes.description: The formal accreditation standard under which this method is certified (e.g., NATA for National Association of Testing Authorities in Australia, ISO 17025 for international laboratory accreditation, A2LA for American Association for Laboratory Accreditation). Critical for resource estimation and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: accuracy_bias_percent
attributes.description: Method accuracy expressed as percentage bias from certified reference material (CRM) true values. Positive values indicate over-reporting; negative values indicate under-reporting. Acceptable bias is typically within ±5% for resource estimation methods.

attributes.name: analysis_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Typical time required to complete the analytical procedure for a single sample, measured in minutes. Used for laboratory capacity planning and turnaround time estimation.

attributes.name: analyte_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of chemical elements or compounds that this method can detect and quantify (e.g., Au, Ag, Cu, Fe, S, C for multi-element methods; Au only for single-element fire assay). Defines the scope of the method's analytical capability.

attributes.name: approved_for_process_control
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this method is approved for real-time or near-real-time process control and optimization in mineral processing plants. True if suitable for operational decision-making; false if restricted to formal assay reporting.

attributes.name: approved_for_resource_estimation
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this method meets the quality and accreditation standards required for JORC, NI 43-101, or SAMREC compliant mineral resource and ore reserve estimation. True if approved; false if restricted to process control or non-compliant applications.

attributes.name: cost_per_sample
attributes.description: Standard cost to analyze one sample using this method, including labor, consumables, reagents, and instrument time. Used for laboratory budgeting and exploration/production cost estimation. Expressed in the organization's reporting currency.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this analytical method record was first created in the LIMS or laboratory management system. Used for audit trails and data lineage.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 Record Management, Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: detection_limit_lower
attributes.description: Minimum concentration or grade that the method can reliably detect and quantify, expressed in the method's reporting unit. Values below this threshold are reported as below detection limit (BDL).

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this method version became active and approved for use in the laboratory. Used for historical data traceability and audit compliance.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this method version was superseded or retired. Null for currently active methods. Used for historical data traceability and method lifecycle management.

attributes.name: instrument_type
attributes.description: Type or model family of analytical instrument required to perform this method (e.g., Varian AA240 Atomic Absorption Spectrometer, Bruker S8 Tiger XRF, Agilent 7900 ICP-MS, LECO CS844 Carbon/Sulphur Analyzer). Used for instrument scheduling and capacity planning.

attributes.name: interference_notes
attributes.description: Documentation of known chemical or spectral interferences that may affect method accuracy (e.g., high iron content interfering with copper XRF analysis, arsenic interference in gold fire assay). Used to guide method selection and result interpretation.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this analytical method record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 Record Management, Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: last_validation_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent method validation or re-validation exercise, including precision and accuracy testing against certified reference materials. ISO 17025 requires periodic re-validation.

attributes.name: matrix_applicability
attributes.description: Description of the sample matrix types for which this method is validated and approved (e.g., oxide ore, sulphide ore, concentrate, tailings, soil, water, rock). Critical for ensuring method suitability for different geological and process materials.

attributes.name: method_category
attributes.description: Business classification of the method's primary application domain (geochemical for ore assays, metallurgical for concentrate and recovery testing, environmental for tailings and water analysis, quality_control for QA/QC samples, process_control for real-time plant monitoring).

attributes.name: method_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code identifying the analytical method (e.g., FA-AAS-01, XRF-PP-02, ICP-MS-03). Used as the business identifier for the method across laboratory systems and resource estimation workflows.

attributes.name: method_documentation_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the detailed method documentation, standard operating procedure (SOP), or published standard (e.g., SOP-LAB-FA-001, ASTM E1915, ISO 11426). Used to access full procedural details and compliance evidence.

attributes.name: method_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the analytical method (e.g., Fire Assay with Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy for Gold, X-Ray Fluorescence Pressed Pellet for Multi-Element Analysis).

attributes.name: method_owner
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the laboratory manager or technical specialist responsible for maintaining and validating this method. Used for accountability and technical queries.

attributes.name: method_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the analytical method. Active methods are approved for use; superseded methods have been replaced by newer versions; pending_accreditation methods are awaiting formal approval.

attributes.name: method_type
attributes.description: Classification of the analytical technique family (e.g., fire_assay for FA-AAS/FA-OES, xrf for X-Ray Fluorescence, icp_ms for Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry, leco for LECO carbon/sulphur analyzers). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fire_assay|xrf|icp_ms|icp_oes|leco|titration|gravimetric|wet_chemistry|spectroscopy|other — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025, Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Standards

attributes.name: method_version
attributes.description: Version number of the analytical method (e.g., 1.0, 2.1, 3.0.1). Incremented when method parameters, detection limits, or procedures are updated.

attributes.name: next_validation_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next method validation or re-validation exercise. Used for laboratory quality management and accreditation maintenance planning.

attributes.name: precision_rsd_percent
attributes.description: Method precision expressed as relative standard deviation (RSD) percentage, derived from replicate analysis of certified reference materials (CRMs). Lower values indicate higher precision. Typical acceptable range is 1-10% depending on analyte and concentration.

attributes.name: reagent_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of chemical reagents required for the analytical procedure (e.g., lithium borate flux, hydrochloric acid, nitric acid, lead oxide, silver nitrate). Used for laboratory inventory management and safety planning.

attributes.name: reference_material_required
attributes.description: Specification of certified reference materials (CRMs) or standard reference materials (SRMs) that must be analyzed alongside samples for quality control (e.g., OREAS 101a, AMIS 0318, NIST 2709a). Critical for QA/QC protocol compliance.

attributes.name: reporting_unit
attributes.description: Standard unit of measure in which analytical results are reported (e.g., ppm for parts per million, g_per_t for grams per tonne, percent for percentage concentration). Aligns with JORC and NI 43-101 reporting standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ppm|ppb|percent|g_per_t|mg_per_l|ug_per_l|oz_per_ton — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: sample_preparation_procedure
attributes.description: Description of the required sample preparation steps before analysis (e.g., crushing to -2mm, pulverizing to 90% passing 75 microns, drying at 105°C, pressed pellet formation, fusion bead preparation). Critical for method reproducibility and quality control.

attributes.name: turnaround_time_hours
attributes.description: Standard turnaround time from sample receipt to result reporting, measured in hours. Includes sample preparation, analysis, quality control, and data validation. Used for mine planning and grade control scheduling.

attributes.name: upper_limit
attributes.description: Maximum concentration or grade that the method can accurately measure without dilution or re-analysis. Samples exceeding this limit require dilution or alternative method.

Stores CRM code, supplier, certificate number, certified values per analyte, uncertainty ranges, matrix type, expiry date, and stock quantity. Ensures traceability of QA/QC performance to internationally recognised standards as required by JORC, NI 43-101, and SAMREC.

attributes.name: crm_standard_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the certified reference material standard record. Primary key for the CRM standard register.
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, NI 43-101, SAMREC Code

attributes.name: analytical_method_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.analytical_method. attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.laboratory. Business justification: CRM standards are characterized (certified values determined) at a specific laboratory. Currently crm_standard has characterization_laboratory (STRING) but no FK. Adding characterization_laboratory_id

attributes.name: chemical_register_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.chemical_register. Business justification: Certified Reference Materials are chemical substances requiring SDS registration, storage management, and disposal tracking under mining WHS regulations. The chemical register entry governs safe handl

attributes.name: commodity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: commodity_type on crm_standard is a denormalization of commodity. CRM standards are certified reference materials for specific commodities (iron ore CRM, copper CRM). Selecting the correct CRM for a b

attributes.name: supplier_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.counterparty. Business justification: Certified reference materials are purchased from specialized suppliers who are counterparties. This link enables purchase order tracking, supplier performance evaluation, certificate verification, inv

attributes.name: certificate_number
attributes.description: Unique certificate or lot number issued by the supplier that identifies the batch of certified reference material and links to the official certificate of analysis.

attributes.name: certification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the reference material was officially certified by the supplier or certifying body, as documented on the certificate of analysis.

attributes.name: certified_value_json
attributes.description: JSON-formatted string containing certified values for all analytes in the reference material, including element symbol, certified concentration, unit of measure, and uncertainty. Structured as array of objects to support multi-element standards.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this certified reference material record was first created in the laboratory information management system (LIMS).

attributes.name: crm_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the certified reference material, typically assigned by the supplier or internal laboratory. Used for sample tracking and quality control workflows.

attributes.name: crm_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name or title of the certified reference material, often including the supplier designation and material type.

attributes.name: crm_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the certified reference material in the laboratory inventory and quality assurance program.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the unit cost of the certified reference material (e.g., USD, AUD, CAD).

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date after which the certified reference material is no longer guaranteed to meet its certified values and should not be used in quality control programs. Nullable for materials with indefinite stability.

attributes.name: homogeneity_statement
attributes.description: Statement or assessment from the supplier regarding the homogeneity of the reference material, indicating whether it is suitable for the intended sample size and analytical method.

attributes.name: is_in_house_standard
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this is an in-house prepared reference material (true) or a commercially sourced certified reference material (false). In-house standards are typically prepared from site-specific ore and characterized through round-robin testing.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this certified reference material record was last updated in the laboratory information management system (LIMS).

attributes.name: matrix_type
attributes.description: Physical and chemical composition category of the reference material matrix, indicating the material type it is designed to represent in quality control programs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ore|concentrate|tailings|soil|rock|pulp|solution — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: minimum_stock_level
attributes.description: Minimum inventory threshold for the certified reference material below which reordering should be triggered to ensure continuity of quality control programs.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional information, special handling instructions, performance observations, or historical notes related to the certified reference material.

attributes.name: particle_size_description
attributes.description: Description of the particle size distribution or preparation state of the reference material (e.g., minus 75 micron pulp, coarse reject, -200 mesh), relevant for ensuring homogeneity and representativeness in quality control.

attributes.name: purchase_order_number
attributes.description: Purchase order number associated with the procurement of this batch of certified reference material, enabling traceability to procurement records and cost allocation.

attributes.name: qaqc_program_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Program Name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the quality assurance and quality control program in which this certified reference material is used (e.g., Exploration QA/QC, Grade Control QA/QC, Metallurgical QA/QC).
attributes.references: JORC Code 2012 Edition, NI 43-101, SAMREC Code

attributes.name: stock_quantity
attributes.description: Current quantity of the certified reference material available in laboratory inventory, measured in the unit specified in stock_unit_of_measure.

attributes.name: stock_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the stock quantity of the certified reference material (e.g., grams, kilograms, vials).

attributes.name: storage_conditions
attributes.description: Required environmental conditions for storing the certified reference material to maintain stability and certified values (e.g., temperature range, humidity control, light protection).

attributes.name: storage_location
attributes.description: Physical location within the laboratory or warehouse where the certified reference material is stored (e.g., cabinet number, shelf, room identifier).

attributes.name: traceability_statement
attributes.description: Statement describing the metrological traceability of the certified values to international measurement standards or reference materials, as required for compliance with ISO/IEC 17025 and resource reporting codes.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025, ISO Guide 35, JORC Code 2012 Edition

attributes.name: uncertainty_json
attributes.description: JSON-formatted string containing measurement uncertainty ranges for each certified analyte, including standard deviation, confidence interval, and uncertainty type (e.g., expanded uncertainty at 95% confidence level).

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: Cost per unit (per gram, vial, or packet) of the certified reference material, used for inventory valuation and budgeting of quality control programs.

attributes.name: usage_frequency
attributes.description: Recommended or actual frequency at which this certified reference material is inserted into the analytical workflow as part of the quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) program.

attributes.name: special_handling_instructions

attributes.name: total_weight_kg

products.name: laboratory
products.description: Master register of all internal and external laboratories used by the mining operation, including on-site preparation laboratories, on-site analytical laboratories, external commercial assay laboratories, and specialist metallurgical test facilities. Stores laboratory name, location, type (preparation, analytical, metallurgical), accreditation body (NATA, SANAS, CALA, A2LA), accreditation number, accreditation expiry, approved analyte and method scope, contracted turnaround time SLA by sample type, cost per sample, preferred laboratory flag, and active/inactive status. Governs laboratory selection rules for different sample types, programs, and priority levels, and supports laboratory performance benchmarking.

products.name: sample_program
products.description: Defines the sampling program or campaign under which samples are collected, such as resource definition drilling, grade control, infill drilling, geotechnical investigation, process plant feed characterisation, metallurgical variability, or environmental monitoring programs. Stores program name, type, associated project or mine area, target commodity, sampling protocol reference, analytical suite specification (which analytes and methods apply), QA/QC insertion rate requirements, start and end date, budget, and responsible geologist or metallurgist. Serves as the governing entity that links samples to their originating business purpose and controls which analytical methods, QA/QC protocols, and turnaround priorities apply to all samples collected under the program.

attributes.name: actual_cycle_time_sec
attributes.description: The measured average time per production unit (e.g., haul cycle, crusher pass) achieved during the period. Compared against ideal_cycle_time_sec to derive Performance Rate. Sourced from MineStar dispatch and OSIsoft PI process historian.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; OSIsoft PI System

attributes.name: actual_operating_time_hrs
attributes.description: Actual hours the asset was in productive operation during the period, after deducting unplanned downtime and breakdowns. Core input to OEE Availability Rate calculation. Sourced from MineStar equipment health and OSIsoft PI historian.
attributes.references: ISO 22400-2; Caterpillar MineStar Equipment Health; OSIsoft PI System

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Username or employee ID of the production supervisor or engineer who approved this OEE record in the reconciliation workflow. Supports audit trail requirements for OPEX reporting and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA PM; Infor EAM; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: availability_rate
attributes.description: The ratio of actual operating time to planned operating time, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.9250 = 92.50%). First component of the OEE composite metric. Calculated as actual_operating_time_hrs / planned_operating_time_hrs. Stored as a raw rate for precision; percentage display handled in reporting layer.
attributes.references: ISO 22400-2; Caterpillar MineStar OEE Module; ICMM Equipment Performance

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for production supervisors or engineers to record contextual notes about this OEE record, such as reasons for low availability, abnormal operating conditions, or data quality caveats.
attributes.references: Infor EAM Work Order Notes; Caterpillar MineStar Shift Reports

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this OEE record was first created in the data platform, either by automated ingestion from MineStar/OSIsoft PI or by manual entry. Supports audit trail and data lineage.
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management; SAP S/4HANA Audit Trail

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the primary operational system from which this OEE record was sourced or reconciled. Supports data lineage tracing and audit of production reconciliation processes.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar; OSIsoft PI System; Infor EAM; SAP S/4HANA

attributes.name: distance_travelled_km
attributes.description: Total distance travelled by mobile fleet assets (e.g., haul trucks, dozers) during the period, in kilometres. Used for tyre wear analysis, fuel efficiency benchmarking, and haul road condition assessment. Not applicable to fixed plant assets.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Fleet Management; Fleet Management System (FMS)

attributes.name: engine_hours
attributes.description: Total engine running hours accumulated by the asset during the period. Used for maintenance scheduling, MTBF calculation, and asset lifecycle management in Infor EAM. Sourced from MineStar equipment health telematics.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Equipment Health; Infor EAM Asset Lifecycle; ISO 55001 Asset Management

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_l
attributes.description: Total diesel fuel consumed by the asset during the period, measured in litres. Used for fuel efficiency analysis, OPEX cost allocation, and carbon emissions reporting. Sourced from MineStar fuel management or SAP MM fuel issue records.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Equipment Health; SAP S/4HANA MM; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

attributes.name: fuel_efficiency_t_per_l
attributes.description: Ratio of actual throughput in tonnes to fuel consumed in litres during the period. Key OPEX efficiency metric for haul trucks and mobile fleet. Enables benchmarking across fleet and identification of underperforming units.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; ICMM Sustainability Reporting; ISO 14001

attributes.name: ideal_cycle_time_sec
attributes.description: The theoretical minimum time required to produce one unit (e.g., one haul cycle, one crusher pass) under optimal conditions. Used as the benchmark denominator in OEE Performance Rate calculation. Sourced from engineering design specifications or MineStar baseline models.
attributes.references: ISO 22400-2; Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; Mine Engineering Standards

attributes.name: is_reconciled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this OEE record has been through the production reconciliation process and validated against shift reports and source system data. Unreconciled records are provisional and should not be used for OPEX reporting.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; SAP S/4HANA PS Production Reconciliation

attributes.name: load_count
attributes.description: Total number of discrete load cycles (e.g., truck loads, shovel passes) completed by the asset during the period. Used for cycle time analysis and Performance Rate validation. Sourced from MineStar dispatch system.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Dispatch; Fleet Management System (FMS)

attributes.name: oee_rate
attributes.description: The composite OEE metric expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.7500 = 75.00%), calculated as the multiplicative product of availability_rate × performance_rate × quality_rate. This is the primary KPI for fleet performance benchmarking, bottleneck identification, and OPEX reporting. Stored as a pre-reconciled rate from the production reconciliation system.
attributes.references: ISO 22400-2; Caterpillar MineStar OEE Module; ICMM Equipment Performance; SAP S/4HANA PM

attributes.name: oee_target_rate
attributes.description: The budgeted or contractually agreed OEE target rate for this asset type and period, expressed as a decimal. Used for variance analysis between actual OEE and planned OEE in OPEX reporting and fleet performance benchmarking.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO Budgeting; ICMM Equipment Performance; Mine Planning Standards

attributes.name: payload_avg_t
attributes.description: Average payload per load cycle in dry metric tonnes during the period. Used to assess truck loading efficiency against rated payload capacity. Sourced from MineStar payload monitoring system (VIMS/PLM).
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; Fleet Management System (FMS)

attributes.name: performance_rate
attributes.description: The ratio of actual production speed to ideal production speed during operating time, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.8750 = 87.50%). Second component of the OEE composite metric. Calculated as (ideal_cycle_time_sec × total_units_produced) / actual_operating_time_hrs. Stored as raw rate.
attributes.references: ISO 22400-2; Caterpillar MineStar OEE Module; ICMM Equipment Performance

attributes.name: period_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time marking the end of the production period for which OEE is calculated. Combined with period_start_timestamp to derive total period duration.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; OSIsoft PI System

attributes.name: period_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time marking the beginning of the production period (shift or sub-shift interval) for which OEE is calculated. Principal business event timestamp for this record. Sourced from MineStar shift dispatch or OSIsoft PI historian.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; OSIsoft PI System

attributes.name: planned_downtime_hrs
attributes.description: Total hours the asset was taken out of service for scheduled preventive maintenance, inspections, or planned shutdowns during the period. Excluded from planned operating time in OEE Availability calculation.

attributes.name: planned_operating_time_hrs
attributes.description: Total scheduled hours the asset was planned to be in productive operation during the period, excluding planned maintenance windows and scheduled downtime. Core input to OEE Availability Rate calculation. Sourced from MineStar shift schedule.
attributes.references: ISO 22400-2 KPIs for Manufacturing Operations Management; Caterpillar MineStar

attributes.name: production_date
attributes.description: Calendar date associated with this OEE record, representing the production day. Used for daily and monthly OEE trend reporting and OPEX period alignment.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA PS Production Scheduling; ICMM Reporting

attributes.name: quality_rate
attributes.description: The ratio of good units produced to total units produced, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.9900 = 99.00%). Third component of the OEE composite metric. Calculated as (total_units_produced - reject_unit_count) / total_units_produced. For mobile fleet assets where quality is not applicable, this defaults to 1.0000.
attributes.references: ISO 22400-2; LabWare LIMS; ICMM Equipment Performance

attributes.name: reconciliation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this OEE record was formally reconciled and approved in the production reconciliation system. Null if is_reconciled is false.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; SAP S/4HANA PS

attributes.name: record_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this OEE record, formatted as OEE-YYYY-MM-NNNNNN. Used for cross-system referencing between MineStar, OSIsoft PI, and SAP PM reporting.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; Infor EAM

attributes.name: record_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this OEE record within the production reconciliation workflow. Draft records are provisional; approved records are used for OPEX reporting and fleet benchmarking.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; Infor EAM

attributes.name: reject_unit_count
attributes.description: Number of production units that did not meet quality specification during the period (e.g., crusher throughput below grade spec, off-spec concentrate batches). Core input to OEE Quality Rate calculation. Applicable primarily to fixed plant assets; set to zero for mobile fleet where quality is not directly measured.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS Quality Control; OSIsoft PI System; ISO 22400-2

attributes.name: speed_avg_kmh
attributes.description: Average travel speed of the mobile asset during the period, in km/h. Used for haul road performance analysis, speed compliance monitoring, and Performance Rate benchmarking. Sourced from MineStar telematics.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Fleet Management; Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) Speed Compliance

attributes.name: throughput_actual_t
attributes.description: Actual mass of material (ore or waste) processed or moved by the asset during the period, measured in dry metric tonnes. Primary quantitative production outcome for the period. Sourced from MineStar payload monitoring or OSIsoft PI belt scale historian.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; OSIsoft PI System; JORC Code

attributes.name: throughput_target_t
attributes.description: Planned or budgeted throughput in dry metric tonnes for this asset during the period. Used for production variance analysis and OEE Performance Rate benchmarking against mine plan.
attributes.references: Hexagon MinePlan Scheduling; Deswik Mine Planning; SAP S/4HANA PS

attributes.name: total_units_produced
attributes.description: Total count of production units (e.g., haul cycles completed, tonnes crushed, loads dispatched) achieved during the period. Used in Performance Rate and Quality Rate calculations. Sourced from MineStar dispatch or OSIsoft PI throughput counters.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; OSIsoft PI System; ISO 22400-2

attributes.name: unplanned_downtime_hrs
attributes.description: Total hours the asset was unavailable due to unplanned breakdowns, mechanical failures, or unscheduled stoppages during the period. Key driver of Availability Rate degradation. Sourced from Infor EAM work order records.
attributes.references: Infor EAM Work Order Management; ISO 22400-2; ICMM OEE Framework

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this OEE record was most recently modified, including reconciliation updates, corrections, or status changes. Supports change tracking and data quality monitoring in the Silver layer.
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management; SAP S/4HANA Audit Trail; Databricks Delta Lake

products.name: downtime_event
products.description: Records each individual equipment downtime event including unplanned breakdowns, planned maintenance windows, standby, and weather delays. Captures start and end timestamps, downtime category, downtime reason code, responsible crew, and impact on production. Used to calculate MTBF and MTTR and to drive maintenance prioritisation.
products.reference: MineStar Equipment Health / Infor EAM Downtime

attributes.name: downtime_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each equipment downtime event record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Work Order / Downtime Event Entity

attributes.name: asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific piece of mining fleet or fixed plant equipment (e.g., haul truck, drill, shovel, conveyor) that experienced the downtime event. Sourced from Infor EAM asset register and Caterpillar MineStar.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Asset Register; Caterpillar MineStar Fleet Management

attributes.name: component_register_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to equipment.component_register. Business justification: Downtime events in mining are frequently caused by specific component failures (e.g., engine failure, hydraulic pump failure, tyre blowout). The downtime_event table currently stores component_code an

attributes.name: cost_centre_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_centre. Business justification: Downtime events have direct cost implications (lost production, maintenance costs) that must be allocated to cost centres for variance analysis and cost performance reporting in mining operations.

attributes.name: functional_location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to maintenance.functional_location. Business justification: Downtime events are attributed to functional locations for bad-actor analysis and maintenance planning. downtime_event.functional_location_code is a denormalized text reference; a proper FK enables lo

attributes.name: hazard_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.hazard. Business justification: Downtime events caused by hazardous conditions (ground instability, electrical faults, gas detection) must reference the specific hazard for risk-based maintenance prioritisation, bow-tie analysis, an

attributes.name: hse_incident_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Incident ID
attributes.description: Reference to the associated HSE incident record in IsoMetrix when is_safety_related is True. Links the downtime event to the formal safety investigation and regulatory reporting workflow. Null when no safety incident is associated.
attributes.references: IsoMetrix — HSE Incident Management; ISO 45001; MSHA

attributes.name: mine_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the mine site or operational location where the downtime event occurred (e.g., open pit, underground, processing plant).
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA — Plant / Functional Location; Caterpillar MineStar

attributes.name: production_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to mine.production_schedule. Business justification: Downtime events record production_tonnes_lost and production_impact_hours, which must be attributed to a production schedule period for schedule variance reporting and forecast updates. Mine planners

attributes.name: regulatory_condition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.regulatory_condition. Business justification: Stop-work orders and compliance breaches (tenement regulatory conditions) directly cause equipment downtime. Mine compliance teams must link downtime events to the specific regulatory condition that t

attributes.name: saleable_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.saleable_product. Business justification: Production loss reporting requires knowing which saleable product was impacted by each downtime event. Fields production_tonnes_lost and production_impact_hours are meaningless without product context

attributes.name: tenement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tenement.tenement. Business justification: Regulatory production-loss reporting to mining authorities requires downtime events to be attributed to the specific tenement licence area affected. Mine compliance teams query downtime directly by te

attributes.name: tsf_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to tailings.tsf. Business justification: Downtime events on TSF-critical equipment (decant pumps, pipeline systems) must be attributed to the specific TSF for dam safety reporting, operational continuity tracking, and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Major repair and overhaul costs exceeding capitalisation thresholds are charged to WBS elements as CAPEX rather than OPEX. Downtime events triggering major component replacements must reference the WB

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Infor EAM maintenance work order raised in response to or associated with this downtime event. Null for non-maintenance downtime categories such as weather or standby.

attributes.name: actual_repair_hours
attributes.description: Actual number of labour hours expended to complete the repair or maintenance activity for this downtime event. Recorded upon event closure. Used to calculate Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) and to benchmark against estimated_repair_hours for continuous improvement.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Work Order Actual Hours; ISO 22400 (MTTR); SAP S/4HANA PM

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this downtime event record was first created in the source system (Infor EAM or Caterpillar MineStar) and ingested into the silver layer. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SLA compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Record Audit; Caterpillar MineStar; ISO 55000

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the maintenance_cost field (e.g., AUD, USD, ZAR). Supports multi-currency operations across international mine sites.

attributes.name: detection_method
attributes.description: Method by which the downtime event was first detected. Operator_report indicates the equipment operator raised the fault. SCADA_alarm indicates detection via OSIsoft PI System or PLC alarm. FMS_alert indicates detection via Caterpillar MineStar Fleet Management System. Condition_monitoring indicates detection via predictive maintenance sensors. Scheduled_inspection indicates detection during a planned inspection round. Third_party_report indicates detection reported by a contractor or external party.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar; OSIsoft PI System (SCADA); Infor EAM — Condition Monitoring

attributes.name: downtime_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the downtime event type. Unplanned breakdown indicates an unexpected mechanical or electrical failure. Planned maintenance covers scheduled preventive or corrective maintenance windows. Standby covers equipment waiting for work assignment. Weather delay covers stoppages due to adverse environmental conditions. Operational delay covers delays caused by operational constraints such as blasting exclusion zones. Process delay covers upstream or downstream process bottlenecks.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Downtime Category; ISO 22400 (OEE Definitions); Caterpillar MineStar

attributes.name: downtime_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardised reason code identifying the specific cause of the downtime event (e.g., engine failure, tyre change, hydraulic leak, conveyor belt tear, electrical fault). Sourced from Infor EAM failure code library and Caterpillar MineStar reason code catalogue. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: engine_failure|tyre_change|hydraulic_leak|conveyor_belt_tear|electrical_fault|structural_damage|operator_error|fuel_system|cooling_system|brake_system — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Failure Code Library; Caterpillar MineStar Reason Codes; ISO 14224 (Reliability Data Collection)

attributes.name: downtime_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the downtime event record. Open indicates the event has been logged but resolution has not commenced. In_progress indicates maintenance or corrective action is underway. Resolved indicates the equipment has been returned to service. Cancelled indicates the event was logged in error. Pending_approval indicates the event record is awaiting supervisory sign-off.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Work Order Status; SAP S/4HANA PM

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed duration of the downtime event expressed in whole minutes, calculated as the difference between end_timestamp and start_timestamp. Stored as a business field to support direct reporting and MTTR calculations without requiring timestamp arithmetic at query time. Null if end_timestamp is not yet recorded.
attributes.references: ISO 22400 — Mean Time To Repair (MTTR); Infor EAM; Caterpillar MineStar

attributes.name: end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the equipment was returned to operational service and the downtime event concluded. Null if the event is still open or in progress. Used in conjunction with start_timestamp to calculate actual downtime duration.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar — Equipment Health; Infor EAM; ISO 22400

attributes.name: environmental_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this downtime event resulted in or had the potential to cause an environmental impact (e.g., hydraulic fluid spill, dust emission exceedance, tailings pump failure). True triggers environmental notification and reporting obligations under ISO 14001 and site Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) conditions.
attributes.references: IsoMetrix — Environmental Monitoring; ISO 14001 (Environmental Management Systems); EIS Conditions

attributes.name: estimated_repair_hours
attributes.description: Estimated number of labour hours required to complete the repair or maintenance activity associated with this downtime event, as assessed at the time of event creation. Used for maintenance scheduling, resource planning, and comparison against actual repair duration to improve future estimates.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Work Order Estimated Hours; SAP S/4HANA PM

attributes.name: event_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description of the downtime event as recorded by the operator or maintenance technician at the time of reporting. Captures contextual details not covered by structured fields, including observed symptoms, environmental conditions, and initial diagnosis. Sourced from Infor EAM notification text or Caterpillar MineStar operator notes.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Notification Long Text; Caterpillar MineStar Operator Notes

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the downtime event, formatted as DT-YYYY-NNNNNN. Used for cross-referencing with Infor EAM work orders, MineStar dispatch logs, and SAP PM notifications. Supports traceability across operational systems.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Downtime Notification Reference; Caterpillar MineStar

attributes.name: failure_mode
attributes.description: Describes the specific manner in which the equipment failed or the mechanism of the downtime (e.g., fatigue fracture, corrosion, overheating, wear, contamination, misalignment). Aligned with ISO 14224 failure mode taxonomy and used in Reliability Centred Maintenance (RCM) analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fatigue_fracture|corrosion|overheating|wear|contamination|misalignment|vibration|leakage|blockage|electrical_short — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO 14224 — Reliability and Maintenance Data Collection; Infor EAM RCM Module

attributes.name: is_safety_related
attributes.description: Indicates whether this downtime event was caused by or resulted in a safety incident, near-miss, or equipment condition that posed a risk to personnel. True triggers mandatory notification to the Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) team and may require IsoMetrix incident reporting. Supports Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) and Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate (TRIFR) compliance reporting.
attributes.references: IsoMetrix — HSE Incident Management; ISO 45001 (Occupational Health and Safety); MSHA Regulations

attributes.name: maintenance_cost
attributes.description: Total direct cost incurred to resolve this downtime event, including labour, parts, and consumables as captured in Infor EAM and SAP S/4HANA CO. Expressed in the site operating currency. Used for Operating Expenditure (OPEX) tracking, cost-per-hour analysis, and maintenance budget variance reporting.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO — Cost Object; Infor EAM — Work Order Cost; IFRS (Operating Expenditure)

attributes.name: maintenance_type
attributes.description: Classification of the maintenance activity associated with this downtime event. Corrective maintenance addresses failures after they occur. Preventive maintenance is time-based scheduled work. Predictive maintenance is triggered by condition monitoring data. Condition-based maintenance is triggered by measured parameter thresholds. Emergency maintenance addresses safety-critical failures requiring immediate response. Null for non-maintenance downtime categories.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Maintenance Type Classification; ISO 14224; ISO 55000 (Asset Management)

attributes.name: oee_impact_category
attributes.description: Classification of how this downtime event impacts the Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) calculation. Availability losses arise from unplanned breakdowns and planned maintenance. Performance losses arise from reduced speed or throughput. Quality losses arise from off-spec production. Used to decompose OEE into its three constituent factors for targeted improvement initiatives.
attributes.references: ISO 22400 — Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE); Caterpillar MineStar; ICMM

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Priority classification assigned to the downtime event to drive maintenance resource allocation and response urgency. Critical indicates immediate safety or production-stopping impact. High indicates significant production impact requiring same-shift response. Medium indicates moderate impact with next-shift response acceptable. Low indicates minor impact with scheduled response acceptable.
attributes.references: Infor EAM — Work Order Priority; SAP S/4HANA PM Priority Classification

attributes.name: production_impact_hours
attributes.description: Estimated or actual number of production hours lost as a direct consequence of this downtime event. Accounts for the impact on the production schedule and is used to quantify the effect on Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) and Life of Mine (LOM) plan adherence. Sourced from Caterpillar MineStar productivity tracking.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar — Productivity Tracking; ISO 22400 (OEE); ICMM Reporting

attributes.name: production_tonnes_lost
attributes.description: Estimated tonnage of ore or material (Run of Mine — ROM) that was not moved or processed as a direct result of this downtime event. Used to quantify the financial and operational impact of equipment unavailability on the mine production schedule.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar — Productivity Tracking; Mine Production Schedule (Deswik/Hexagon MinePlan)

attributes.name: resolution_notes
