attributes.name: recommended_pressure_kpa
attributes.description: OEM-recommended cold inflation pressure in kilopascals (kPa) for this tyre size and load rating. Reference value for pressure compliance checks and deviation alerting.
attributes.references: OEM tyre specification sheets; TRA (Tire and Rim Association)

attributes.name: recorded_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this tyre record was first created in the system, representing the record audit creation time. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: Infor EAM; Kal Tire TOMS; ISO 8601

attributes.name: removal_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the tyre was removed from the vehicle. Null if the tyre is currently in service. Combined with installation_date to calculate service duration.
attributes.references: Infor EAM Work Orders; Kal Tire TOMS

attributes.name: removal_reason
attributes.description: Reason code for tyre removal from service. Drives failure mode analysis, vendor performance benchmarking, and haul road condition assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: worn|damaged|rotated|scrapped|puncture|sidewall_failure|heat_separation|scheduled_change|bead_damage|cut — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Kal Tire TOMS; Klinge Tyre Management System; ICMM Good Practice Guide

attributes.name: retread_count
attributes.description: Number of times this tyre carcass has been retreaded. Tracks carcass reuse for cost optimisation and quality assurance. OEM carcass inspection standards typically limit retreads to 1-2 cycles for large OTR tyres.
attributes.references: Kal Tire TOMS; Klinge Tyre Management System; TRA (Tire and Rim Association)

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer-assigned unique serial number stamped on the tyre sidewall. Used as the primary physical identifier for tyre tracking across its full lifecycle from receipt to disposal.
attributes.references: Kal Tire TOMS; Klinge Tyre Management System; ISO 10012

attributes.name: size_specification
attributes.description: Standard tyre size designation in OEM format (e.g., 40.00R57, 27.00R49, 37.00R57). Encodes width, aspect ratio, and rim diameter per TRA/ETRTO standards. Critical for procurement and fitment compatibility.
attributes.references: TRA (Tire and Rim Association); ETRTO (European Tyre and Rim Technical Organisation)

attributes.name: speed_rating_kmh
attributes.description: Maximum permissible operating speed in kilometres per hour as specified by the OEM. Relevant for haul road speed limit compliance and tyre selection for high-speed haulage applications.
attributes.references: TRA (Tire and Rim Association); OEM tyre specification sheets

attributes.name: tkph_actual
attributes.description: Calculated actual TKPH value based on the haul truck payload, haul road distance, and cycle time recorded by Caterpillar MineStar. Compared against tkph_rating to assess thermal overload risk.
attributes.references: Caterpillar MineStar Productivity Tracking; TRA TKPH Guidelines

attributes.name: tkph_rating
attributes.description: OEM-specified Tonne-Kilometres Per Hour (TKPH) rating for the tyre, representing the maximum thermal load the tyre can sustain. Compliance with TKPH rating is critical to prevent heat-related tyre failures in open-cut mining haul cycles.
attributes.references: TRA (Tire and Rim Association); Bridgestone/Michelin TKPH Guidelines; ICMM Good Practice Guide

attributes.name: tread_depth_current_mm
attributes.description: Most recent tread depth measurement in millimetres recorded at the last inspection. Used to assess remaining tyre life and trigger rotation or replacement decisions.
attributes.references: Kal Tire TOMS; Klinge Tyre Management System; ICMM Good Practice Guide

attributes.name: tread_depth_new_mm
attributes.description: Original tread depth in millimetres when the tyre was new, as specified by the OEM. Baseline reference for calculating tread wear percentage and remaining tread life.
attributes.references: TRA (Tire and Rim Association); OEM tyre specification sheets

attributes.name: tread_depth_removal_mm
attributes.description: Tread depth in millimetres measured at the time of tyre removal. Null if tyre is still in service. Used to determine whether the tyre reached its designed wear limit or was removed prematurely.
attributes.references: Kal Tire TOMS; Klinge Tyre Management System

attributes.name: tyre_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the tyre. Tracks whether the tyre is actively mounted, held in the tyre bay, undergoing repair/retread, scrapped, or disposed. Supports inventory management and lifecycle cost analysis.
attributes.references: Infor EAM Asset Lifecycle; Kal Tire TOMS

attributes.name: tyre_type
attributes.description: Tyre construction category indicating internal structure. Radial is standard for large haul trucks; bias ply used on some older or smaller equipment; solid and foam-filled used in specific underground or loader applications.
attributes.references: TRA (Tire and Rim Association); Kal Tire TOMS

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this tyre record, capturing inspection results, status changes, or measurement updates. Supports incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: Infor EAM; Kal Tire TOMS; ISO 8601

attributes.name: warranty_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the OEM or supplier warranty for this tyre expires. Enables timely warranty claims for premature failures and supports procurement negotiations with tyre vendors.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA MM Warranty Management; Pronto Xi Procurement

domains.name: maintenance
domains.description: Manages the full asset maintenance lifecycle including preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance work orders, BOM, spare parts consumption, shutdown planning, and equipment downtime tracking via CMMS (Infor EAM). Owns work execution and cost history against each asset.

products.name: work_order
products.description: Core transactional entity representing a maintenance work order in Infor EAM. Captures all types of maintenance activities — preventive (PM), corrective (CM), predictive (PdM), and condition-based — against a specific asset. Tracks work order number, type, priority, status, originating source (CMMS, SCADA alert, operator request), planned vs actual start/finish dates, estimated vs actual labour hours, work centre, trade/craft required, safety permit references, shutdown flag, and completion codes. Includes full cost summary: labour cost, parts/materials cost, contractor cost, equipment hire cost, total estimated vs actual cost (OPEX), cost centre, GL account code, SAP CO order reference, cost variance, and approval status. SSOT for work execution history and maintenance cost reporting against each asset. Supports AISC/C1 cost allocation. Sourced from Infor EAM and SAP CO.

attributes.name: last_completion_date

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: last_review_date

attributes.name: next_due_date
attributes.description: The calculated date when the next preventive maintenance work order is due to be generated and executed. Automatically calculated based on last_completion_date and interval_value.

attributes.name: next_review_date

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or context about this PM schedule. May include historical information, change rationale, or operational considerations.

attributes.name: permit_required_flag

attributes.name: plan_description

attributes.name: pm_plan_code

attributes.name: review_cycle_months

attributes.name: source_system

attributes.name: source_system_code

products.name: shutdown_plan
products.description: Master record for a planned maintenance shutdown or major overhaul event at a mine site or processing plant, including all scope items and work packages. Header captures shutdown name, type (annual shutdown, major overhaul, statutory inspection), planned and actual start/end dates, scope description, responsible superintendent, total planned duration and cost (CAPEX/OPEX), shutdown status, and project code. Scope line items capture individual work packages: scope item number, description, asset/functional location, trade required, estimated hours and cost, priority, critical path flag, predecessor items, and completion status. Enables shutdown scope management, resource levelling, and critical path scheduling. Sourced from Infor EAM and SAP PS.

products.description: Record of condition monitoring readings, predictive measurements, and inspection rounds performed on an asset to support predictive and condition-based maintenance. Captures asset ID, monitoring type (vibration analysis, thermography, oil analysis, ultrasonic, visual inspection, wear measurement, operator inspection round), measurement date, measured value or pass/fail result, unit of measure, baseline value, alarm threshold, alert level (normal/warning/critical), technician/inspector ID, instrument used, trend direction, defects identified, defect severity, and recommended action or follow-up work order flag. products.name: job_plan_parts_list
products.description: This association product represents the pre-approved Bill of Materials (BOM) for a Standard Job Plan in the CMMS. It captures the specific spare parts required to execute a standard job plan, along with the quantity, unit of measure, staging sequence, and criticality context for each part-job combination. Each record links one standard_job to one spare_part and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific job-part pairing. This entity drives parts reservation, kitting, and procurement planning for scheduled and preventive maintenance activities. Sourced from Infor EAM job plan material lines.. Existence Justification: In CMMS/EAM systems like Infor EAM, a Standard Job Plan (SJP) has a pre-approved Bill of Materials (parts list) that maintenance planners actively manage — adding, removing, and adjusting quantities of spare parts per job plan. A single standard job plan requires many spare parts, and a single spare part appears on many different standard job plans. This is the 'Standard Job Parts List' or 'Job Plan Material List', a first-class operational entity that drives parts reservation, kitting, and procurement planning for scheduled maintenance.

attributes.name: criticality_classification
attributes.description: The criticality classification of this spare part in the context of this specific job plan execution (e.g., critical, insurance, non-critical). May differ from the spare part's general criticality_classification on the spare_part master, as a part may be critical for one job plan but non-critical for another.

attributes.name: parts_list_attached_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Bill of Materials (BOM) or parts list is attached to this job plan, specifying required spare parts and consumables. Once the job_plan_parts_list association table is created, the existence of records in that table makes this flag redundant and derivable. It should be deprecated from standard_job in favour of the association table.]
attributes.references: Infor EAM BOM / SAP PM Material List

attributes.name: quantity_required
attributes.description: The quantity of this spare part required to execute one instance of the standard job plan. Belongs to the job-part relationship, not to either entity alone — the same part may be required in different quantities on different job plans.
attributes.references: Infor EAM Job Plan Material Line — Quantity field

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: The order in which this part should be staged or kitted when preparing materials for job execution. Used by stores and kitting teams to assemble parts in the correct sequence for the job plan. Belongs to the relationship, not to the part or job plan independently.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the quantity_required field (e.g., EA, KG, L, M). Defined at the job-plan-part level as the UOM may differ from the spare part's default stocking UOM in specific job contexts.

domains.name: tailings
domains.description: Governs tailings storage facility (TSF) operations, waste rock management, geotechnical monitoring, and rehabilitation planning. Tracks dam safety, seepage, raise schedules, and closure liabilities in compliance with ICMM Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management and EIS requirements.

Drives dam safety review frequency and design standards.

products.name: dam_safety_inspection
products.description: Records formal dam safety inspections and geotechnical stability analyses conducted on TSFs and waste rock embankments. For inspections: captures inspection type (routine, annual, independent review, ITRB), inspector identity and credentials, inspection date, overall safety rating, freeboard measurement, seepage observations, slope condition, instrumentation status, and required remedial actions. For stability analyses: captures analysis type (static, pseudo-static, dynamic), software used, failure mode assessed, factor of safety (FoS) calculated, phreatic surface assumptions, material strength parameters, and engineer of record sign-off. Supports compliance with ANCOLD, CDA, MAC, USACE, and ICMM GISTM Requirements 5 (EoR), 10 (design basis), and 11 (dam safety review) including minimum FoS obligations.

products.name: deposition
products.description: Records tailings deposition events and periodic volumetric capacity surveys for TSFs. For deposition: captures volume deposited, slurry density, solids tonnage, deposition point location, spigot configuration, beach length, pond level, and freeboard at time of deposition. For capacity surveys: captures survey date, survey method (drone photogrammetry, LiDAR, GPS), total storage capacity, remaining airspace, current storage volume, beach elevation, and pond surface area. SSOT for TSF filling status and remaining life calculations. Tracks operational filling against the approved deposition plan and capacity model, informing raise scheduling and operational planning. Supports GISTM Requirement 12 (management and operations).

products.name: water_balance
products.description: Periodic water balance calculations and decant operation records for TSFs and associated water management infrastructure. For water balance: captures all inflows (process water, rainfall, runoff, groundwater ingress), outflows (evaporation, seepage, decant return, spillway discharge), storage volumes, pond levels, freeboard, and reconciliation against design assumptions. For decant operations: captures decant event date, decant structure used (penstock, decant tower, pump), volume decanted, water quality at point of decant, destination (process water return, evaporation pond, treatment plant), and compliance with water licence conditions. SSOT for TSF water management including return water quality. Supports water licence compliance, TSF operational planning, and GISTM Requirement 12 (management of water).

attributes.description: Volume of water stored in the TSF pond at the start of the balance period, measured in cubic meters. Derived from pond level survey and storage-elevation relationship.

attributes.name: process_water_inflow_m3
attributes.description: Volume of process water discharged to the TSF from mineral processing operations during the balance period, measured in cubic meters. Includes tailings slurry water and any additional process water streams.

attributes.name: rainfall_inflow_m3
attributes.description: Volume of direct rainfall onto the TSF pond surface during the balance period, calculated from rainfall depth and pond area, measured in cubic meters.

attributes.name: reviewed_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the person who reviewed and validated the water balance calculation. Ensures quality control and technical oversight of water management data.

attributes.name: runoff_inflow_m3
attributes.description: Volume of surface water runoff from the TSF catchment area entering the pond during the balance period, measured in cubic meters. Includes runoff from embankment slopes and upstream catchment if not diverted.

attributes.name: seepage_outflow_m3
attributes.description: Volume of water lost through seepage from the TSF embankment and foundation during the balance period, measured in cubic meters. Estimated from piezometric data, seepage collection systems, and geotechnical models.

attributes.name: spillway_discharge_outflow_m3
attributes.description: Volume of water discharged through the TSF spillway during the balance period, measured in cubic meters. Typically occurs during extreme rainfall events when pond capacity is exceeded.

attributes.name: storage_change_m3
attributes.description: Net change in water storage volume during the balance period, measured in cubic meters. Calculated as closing storage minus opening storage. Should reconcile with total inflow minus total outflow.

attributes.name: total_inflow_m3
attributes.description: Sum of all water inflows to the TSF during the balance period, measured in cubic meters. Calculated as process water + rainfall + runoff + groundwater + other inflows.

attributes.name: total_outflow_m3
attributes.description: Sum of all water outflows from the TSF during the balance period, measured in cubic meters. Calculated as evaporation + seepage + decant return + spillway discharge + other outflows.

attributes.description: Assessment of whether the water balance period operations complied with water licence conditions including discharge limits, return water quality, and reporting requirements.

domains.name: hse
domains.description: Manages health, safety, and environmental compliance including incident reporting, LTIFR/TRIFR tracking, risk assessments, environmental monitoring, permit conditions, PPE tracking, and regulatory submissions. Integrates IsoMetrix for HSE event management and supports ISO 45001, ISO 14001, MSHA, and GRI reporting.

products.name: incident
products.description: Master record of all health, safety, and environmental incidents and their investigations at mine sites. Covers injuries (LTI, MTI, FAI, RWI), near-misses, environmental spills, unauthorized discharges, permit exceedances, heritage disturbances, and biodiversity impacts. Captures incident type, severity classification, LTIFR/TRIFR contribution flags, affected media (for environmental events), location, shift, activity being performed, immediate causes, containment actions, remediation requirements, and regulatory notification status. For investigated incidents, records root cause analysis methodology (ICAM, Bow-Tie, 5-Why), contributing factors, immediate and underlying causes, investigation team members, and final investigation report status. Tracks regulatory submission deadlines for MSHA and state authority notifications. Sourced from IsoMetrix HSE event management. SSOT for ALL HSE incident records and their formal investigations.
products.reference: IsoMetrix Incident Management / ISO 45001 / MSHA Part 50

products.name: emergency_response_plan

Supports ISO 45001 Clause 8.2 and MSHA emergency response requirements.

attributes.name: cas_number
attributes.description: Unique numerical identifier assigned by the Chemical Abstracts Service to every chemical substance described in the open scientific literature.

attributes.name: chemical_name
attributes.description: Common or trade name of the hazardous chemical or substance as used in operations (e.g., Sodium Cyanide, Sulphuric Acid, Xanthate, ANFO).
attributes.references: GHS Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling

attributes.name: chemical_register_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the chemical in the register (active = currently in use, inactive = no longer used but may have residual inventory, restricted = use limited by permit or policy, phased_out = scheduled for elimination, pending_approval = awaiting regulatory or management approval).

attributes.name: chemical_type
attributes.description: Classification of the chemical based on its primary use or function in mining operations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: reagent|explosive_precursor|fuel|solvent|acid|base|oxidizer|process_chemical — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the chemical register record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: current_inventory_quantity
attributes.description: Current quantity of the chemical on hand at the site, as of the last inventory count or system update.

attributes.name: disposal_method
attributes.description: Approved method for disposal of the chemical or its waste residues (e.g., Licensed Hazardous Waste Contractor, Neutralization and Discharge, Return to Supplier, Incineration).
attributes.references: ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems, RCRA Resource Conservation and Recovery Act

attributes.name: emergency_contact_number
attributes.description: 24-hour emergency contact phone number for the chemical supplier or emergency response service (e.g., CHEMTREC, supplier hotline).

attributes.name: environmental_impact_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes describing known or potential environmental impacts of the chemical, including aquatic toxicity, persistence, bioaccumulation, or soil contamination risks.
attributes.references: ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems, GRI Global Reporting Initiative

attributes.name: first_registered_date
attributes.description: Date when the chemical was first registered in the site chemical register.

attributes.name: ghs_classification
attributes.description: Hazard classification code(s) according to the GHS standard (e.g., Acute Toxicity Category 2, Corrosive to Metals Category 1, Environmental Hazard Acute Category 1).
attributes.references: GHS Rev.9 - UN Globally Harmonized System

attributes.name: ghs_pictogram_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of GHS pictogram codes representing hazard symbols (e.g., GHS05 for Corrosion, GHS06 for Skull and Crossbones, GHS09 for Environment).
attributes.references: GHS Rev.9 - UN Globally Harmonized System

attributes.name: handling_procedure_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or title of the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) governing safe handling, use, and storage of this chemical.
attributes.references: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management

attributes.name: hazard_statement_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of H-codes describing the nature of hazards (e.g., H290 May be corrosive to metals, H314 Causes severe skin burns and eye damage, H400 Very toxic to aquatic life).
attributes.references: GHS Rev.9 - UN Globally Harmonized System

attributes.name: health_hazard_summary
attributes.description: Summary of primary health hazards associated with exposure to this chemical (e.g., Corrosive to skin and eyes, Respiratory irritant, Carcinogen Category 1A, Acute toxicity if ingested).

attributes.name: incompatible_materials
attributes.description: List of materials or chemical classes that must not be stored or mixed with this chemical due to risk of dangerous reactions (e.g., Strong oxidizers, Acids, Alkalis, Water-reactive substances).

attributes.name: inventory_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the maximum inventory quantity (e.g., kilograms, litres, tonnes, cubic metres, units).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the chemical register record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: Date when the chemical register entry was last reviewed for accuracy and compliance.

attributes.name: maximum_inventory_quantity
attributes.description: Maximum quantity of the chemical permitted to be stored on site at any time, as defined by permit conditions or internal risk assessments.
attributes.references: ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems, MSHA Part 47

attributes.name: next_review_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next mandatory review of this chemical register entry.

attributes.name: ppe_requirements
attributes.description: Mandatory personal protective equipment required when handling this chemical (e.g., Chemical-resistant gloves, Face shield, Respirator with organic vapor cartridge, Acid-resistant apron).
attributes.references: MSHA Part 56/57 Safety and Health Standards, ISO 45001

attributes.name: precautionary_statement_codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of P-codes describing recommended measures to minimize or prevent adverse effects (e.g., P280 Wear protective gloves, P305+P351+P338 IF IN EYES rinse cautiously with water).
attributes.references: GHS Rev.9 - UN Globally Harmonized System

attributes.name: regulatory_threshold_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the chemical quantity exceeds regulatory reporting thresholds (e.g., EPCRA Section 312 Tier II, state environmental reporting).
attributes.references: EPCRA Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act, ISO 14001

attributes.name: regulatory_threshold_type
attributes.description: Description of the specific regulatory threshold or reporting requirement triggered (e.g., EPCRA Tier II Reporting, State Hazardous Substance Inventory).
attributes.references: EPCRA Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act

attributes.name: sds_reference_number
attributes.description: Document control number or identifier for the current Safety Data Sheet (formerly MSDS) on file for this chemical.
attributes.references: MSHA Part 47 Hazard Communication, ISO 11014 SDS

attributes.name: sds_revision_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent revision of the Safety Data Sheet for this chemical.
attributes.references: MSHA Part 47 Hazard Communication, ISO 11014 SDS

attributes.name: storage_area_type
attributes.description: Classification of the storage facility based on its design and environmental controls.
attributes.references: MSHA Part 56/57 Safety and Health Standards

attributes.name: un_number
attributes.description: Four-digit number that identifies hazardous substances in the framework of international transport (e.g., UN1789 for Hydrochloric Acid).
attributes.references: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: usage_purpose
attributes.description: Description of the primary operational purpose or process for which the chemical is used (e.g., Gold leaching, Flotation reagent, Blasting agent, Equipment lubrication, Dust suppression).

attributes.name: waste_classification_code
attributes.description: Regulatory waste classification code for disposal purposes (e.g., EPA Hazardous Waste Code, Basel Convention Code).
attributes.references: RCRA Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, Basel Convention

products.name: audit
products.description: Records of all formal HSE management system audits and field-level compliance assessments including internal audits, third-party certification audits (ISO 45001, ISO 14001), regulatory compliance audits, ICMM performance audits, planned workplace inspections, pre-start equipment checks, statutory inspections, and unplanned field inspections. Captures assessment type discriminator (audit/inspection), scope, assessor/inspector details, checklist items, findings (conformances, non-conformances, observations), corrective action requirements, and certification outcome where applicable. SSOT for all HSE compliance verification activities. Supports MSHA inspection readiness, ISO 45001 internal audit programs, and field-level compliance verification.
products.reference: ISO 45001 Clause 9.2 / ISO 14001 Clause 9.2 / ICMM Health and Safety Performance

products.name: hazard
products.description: Master reference table for hazard. Referenced by hazard_id.

attributes.name: hazard_id
attributes.description: Primary key for hazard

attributes.name: commodity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: Hazards in mining are fundamentally commodity-specific — methane gas and spontaneous combustion for coal, silica dust for iron ore, acid mine drainage for copper/nickel, thermal runaway for lithium. H

attributes.name: parent_hazard_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on hazard (parent_hazard_id)

attributes.name: affected_job_roles
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or description of the job roles, occupations, or worker categories that are exposed to or may encounter this hazard during their work activities (e.g., 'drill operators', 'blasters', 'maintenance technicians', 'haul truck drivers').

attributes.name: affected_work_areas
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or description of the specific work areas, zones, or operational locations within the mine site where this hazard is present or may be encountered (e.g., 'underground stopes', 'processing plant', 'haul roads', 'maintenance workshop').

attributes.name: control_hierarchy_level
attributes.description: The primary level of control applied to manage this hazard according to the hierarchy of controls: elimination (remove hazard), substitution (replace with less hazardous), engineering controls (isolate people from hazard), administrative controls (change work practices), or personal protective equipment (PPE).

attributes.name: control_measures
attributes.description: Detailed description of the specific control measures, safeguards, or mitigation strategies implemented to reduce or eliminate the risk associated with this hazard.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this hazard record was first created in the HSE management system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this hazard definition and its associated controls became effective and applicable in the organization's health and safety management system.

attributes.name: emergency_response_procedure
attributes.description: Summary or reference to the emergency response procedures, first aid measures, or incident response protocols to be followed if an incident involving this hazard occurs.

attributes.name: exposure_limit
attributes.description: The maximum permissible exposure level or threshold limit value for this hazard, including units of measure (e.g., '0.05 mg/m³ for respirable crystalline silica', '85 dBA for noise'). Applicable primarily to chemical, physical, and environmental hazards.

attributes.name: gri_disclosure_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the applicable GRI disclosure standard or indicator related to this hazard, used for sustainability and ESG reporting (e.g., 'GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety').

attributes.name: hazard_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the hazard into major categories: physical (noise, vibration, radiation), chemical (dust, fumes, gases), biological (bacteria, viruses), ergonomic (repetitive strain, manual handling), psychosocial (stress, fatigue), or environmental (spills, emissions).

attributes.name: hazard_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the hazard type for reporting and classification purposes. Follows organizational hazard coding taxonomy.

attributes.name: hazard_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the hazard, including its nature, potential sources, and circumstances under which it may be encountered in mining operations.

attributes.name: hazard_name
attributes.description: The common business name or title of the hazard used for identification and communication across the organization.

attributes.name: hazard_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the hazard record. Active indicates the hazard is currently recognized and managed; under review indicates reassessment is in progress; retired indicates the hazard is no longer present; superseded indicates the hazard definition has been replaced by a newer version.

attributes.name: hazard_type
attributes.description: Specific sub-classification or detailed type of hazard within the broader category (e.g., 'Silica Dust', 'Ground Instability', 'Heavy Equipment Operation', 'Confined Space').

attributes.name: is_reportable
attributes.description: Indicates whether incidents involving this hazard must be reported to external regulatory authorities such as MSHA, state mining departments, or environmental agencies. True if reportable, False otherwise.

attributes.name: last_incident_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent recorded incident, injury, or near-miss event associated with this hazard. Used for trend analysis and control effectiveness evaluation.

attributes.name: likelihood_rating
attributes.description: The probability or frequency with which the hazard is expected to cause harm, ranging from almost certain (expected to occur frequently) to rare (may occur only in exceptional circumstances).

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this hazard record was last updated or modified. Supports change tracking and audit trail.

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: The required or recommended frequency for monitoring, inspecting, or reassessing this hazard to ensure controls remain effective and exposure remains within acceptable limits.

attributes.name: permit_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a work permit, hot work permit, confined space entry permit, or other authorization is required before work involving this hazard can commence. True if permit is mandatory, False otherwise.

attributes.name: ppe_required
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of personal protective equipment required when working in the presence of this hazard (e.g., 'hard hat', 'safety glasses', 'respirator', 'hearing protection', 'high-visibility vest', 'steel-toed boots').

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Citation of applicable mining safety regulations, standards, or legal requirements that govern the management of this hazard (e.g., MSHA 30 CFR Part 56, state mining acts, ISO standards).

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next formal review or reassessment of this hazard and its control measures to ensure continued relevance and effectiveness.

attributes.name: risk_rating
attributes.description: Overall risk level derived from the combination of severity and likelihood, used to prioritize control measures and management attention. Extreme and high risks require immediate action.

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: The potential severity of harm or consequence if the hazard materializes, rated from catastrophic (fatality or permanent total disability) to minor (first aid injury).

attributes.name: training_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether specific safety training or competency certification is required for workers who may be exposed to this hazard. True if training is mandatory, False otherwise.
